# Seniors of NY, full reference

> Key facts and answers from every guide on https://seniorsofny.com. Each guide was checked against official New York State and federal sources on the date shown. Not a government agency.

## EPIC in New York: lower drug costs for people 65 and older

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/epic-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

EPIC is New York's drug coverage program for people 65 and older. It works with Medicare Part D to bring most prescriptions down to $3 to $20. Here is who qualifies and how to apply.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get my mom help paying for prescriptions in Queens?
A: If she is 65 or older, has a Part D plan and income up to $75,000 (or $100,000 with a spouse), she can join EPIC. Apply online at nyepic.primetherapeutics.com or call 1-800-332-3742. Ask EPIC to apply for Extra Help at the same time.

Q: My dad in Buffalo has a Medicare Advantage plan. Can he still use EPIC?
A: Yes, if his Medicare Advantage plan includes Part D drug coverage. EPIC requires Part D, either a stand-alone plan or a Medicare Advantage HMO plan that includes it.

Q: Can I get EPIC if I have Medicaid?
A: Not if you get full Medicaid benefits. People on Medicaid spenddown can be EPIC members, and they pay no EPIC fees.

Q: Do I have to send tax returns with the EPIC application?
A: No. EPIC checks your income with the Social Security Administration and the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance. Use last year's income when you fill out the form.

Q: When can I join EPIC?
A: Any time of year. Joining also gives you a Special Enrollment Period to sign up for a Part D plan if you do not have one.

Q: What is the EPIC phone number?
A: The EPIC Helpline is 1-800-332-3742 (TTY 1-800-290-9138), open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday.

Sources: 

## Extra Help for Medicare drug costs in New York: 2027 guide

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/extra-help-medicare-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

Extra Help cuts Part D costs to a few dollars a prescription. Many New Yorkers get it automatically through the Medicare Savings Program, even with savings. Here is how.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get Extra Help for my mom in the Bronx if she has savings?
A: Apply to HRA for the Medicare Savings Program. New York does not count savings for it, and people who qualify get Extra Help automatically. Call the HRA Medicaid Helpline at 1-888-692-6116.

Q: My dad in Syracuse just got EPIC. Does he still need Extra Help?
A: Yes, if his income is low enough. EPIC requires income-eligible members to apply, and Extra Help members pay no EPIC fees and get lower EPIC copays.

Q: What are the Extra Help copays for 2027?
A: Medicare says up to $5.80 for each generic drug and up to $14.40 for each brand-name drug, with a $0 deductible. After drug costs reach $2,400, you pay $0 for covered drugs.

Q: What are the Extra Help income limits?
A: For 2026, Medicare lists $23,940 in yearly income and $18,090 in resources for a single person, and $32,460 and $36,100 for a married couple.

Q: Do I get Extra Help automatically?
A: Yes, if you get full Medicaid, a Medicare Savings Program, or SSI. Otherwise, apply through Social Security online or at 1-800-772-1213.

Q: Can I apply for Extra Help any time?
A: Yes. Social Security says you can apply for Extra Help any time, before or after you enroll in Part D.

Sources: 

## Free and discounted things for older New Yorkers

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/free-and-discounted-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

Turning 62, 65 and 70 in New York opens up real savings. Here are the free state park days, half-price transit, cheap hunting and fishing licenses, federal park passes, train discounts and free museum options, with the official rules for each.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Can my mom get into state parks on Long Island free because she is over 62?
A: On non-holiday weekdays, yes at most parks. The Golden Park Program gives New York residents 62 and older free vehicle entry to most state parks. She shows her New York driver license or non-driver ID at the gate. A short list of sites is excluded, so check the Golden Park page first.

Q: How does my dad in the Bronx get a senior MetroCard or OMNY card?
A: He can get a Reduced-Fare card at 65. The fastest way is an MTA Customer Service Center or Mobile Sales van, where seniors may get a card the same day. He can also mail the application with a photo and ID copy, which can take up to three months.

Q: How much is the MTA senior fare?
A: Reduced fare is $1.50 for the subway, Staten Island Railway and local, limited and Select buses. Express buses are $3.60 outside weekday rush hours.

Q: At what age is a New York fishing license $5?
A: New York residents 70 and older pay $5 for a fishing, hunting or trapping license. Bowhunting and muzzleloading privileges are free with the $5 base hunting license.

Q: How much is the national parks senior pass?
A: U.S. citizens and permanent residents 62 and older pay $20 for an annual Senior Pass or $80 for a lifetime pass. It covers entrance fees at federal recreation sites.

Q: Does Amtrak have a senior discount?
A: Yes. Travelers 65 and older get 10% off most fares on most trains. Sleeping accommodations are not discounted, and you need proof of age when buying and onboard.

Sources: 

## HEAP in New York for 2026 to 2027: heating help for older adults

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/heap-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

New York's Home Energy Assistance Program opened November 2, 2026 and can pay up to $1,086 toward heat. Households with someone 60 or older get extra. Here is who qualifies, how to apply in NYC and the rest of the state, and the utility discounts that come with it.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: When does HEAP open for 2026 to 2027?
A: The Regular benefit opened November 2, 2026. Emergency HEAP opens January 4, 2027. HERR, the furnace repair and replacement benefit, opened October 1, 2026.

Q: What is the HEAP income limit for one person in New York?
A: For the 2026 to 2027 season, a one-person household can have gross monthly income up to $3,563. For two people the limit is $4,659.

Q: How do I apply for HEAP for my mom in Queens?
A: Apply online through ACCESS NYC (ACCESS HRA), in person at an HRA HEAP office, or by mail to HRA/HEAP, PO Box 1401, Church Street Station, New York, NY 10008. Call 718-557-1399 with questions or for an emergency.

Q: My dad's furnace in Syracuse stopped working. Can HEAP help?
A: If he owns the home, he can apply to Onondaga County DSS for HEAP Heating Equipment Repair and Replacement. HRA lists the benefit at up to $4,000 for a repair or $8,000 for a replacement, once every ten years.

Q: Do seniors get more from HEAP?
A: Yes. A household with someone 60 or older gets an extra $35 on the Regular benefit, and Emergency HEAP allows up to $3,750 in resources instead of $2,500.

Q: Does HEAP lower my monthly electric bill too?
A: HEAP households are automatically enrolled in the Energy Affordability Program, a monthly discount from New York's large gas and electric utilities that can save up to $500 a year.

Sources: 

## Medicaid for New Yorkers 65 and older: 2026 limits and how to apply

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/medicaid-ny-seniors/
Updated: 2026-11-25

Medicaid pays for home care and nursing home care for many older New Yorkers. Here are the 2026 limits, the lookback, Managed Long Term Care, spenddown and where to apply.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get my dad on Medicaid for home care in Staten Island?
A: Apply to HRA, which takes Medicaid applications from New York City residents 65 and older. Once he has Medicaid, call the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350 to request the assessment needed to join a Managed Long Term Care plan.

Q: My mom in Westchester has too much income for Medicaid. Can she still get home care?
A: Possibly. New York's spenddown program lets her qualify once her medical bills reach the amount she is over the limit, and a pooled trust can shelter excess income. Apply through Westchester County DSS at 914-995-3333.

Q: What is the Medicaid income limit for seniors in New York in 2026?
A: $1,836 a month for a single person and $2,489 for a couple, or $1,856 and $2,509 counting the $20 disregard. The resource limit is $33,038 single and $44,796 for a couple.

Q: How far back does Medicaid look for nursing home care in New York?
A: 60 months. Gifts or transfers for less than fair value in that period can cause a penalty period when Medicaid will not pay for nursing home care.

Q: Who must join a Managed Long Term Care plan?
A: People with both Medicare and Medicaid who are 21 or older and need community-based long-term care for more than 120 days. Plans include partially capitated MLTC, PACE and Medicaid Advantage Plus.

Q: Have the 2027 Medicaid limits been released?
A: Not as of November 25, 2026. New York ties the limits to the federal poverty guidelines, which usually come out early in the year.

Sources: 

## Medicare Savings Program in New York: 2026 limits and how to apply

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/medicare-savings-program-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

New York will pay your Medicare Part B premium if your income is under the limit, and it does not count your savings. Here are the 2026 limits, what QMB and QI pay, and where to apply.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get the state to pay my mom's Medicare premium in Brooklyn?
A: Apply to HRA for the Medicare Savings Program. You can apply online through ACCESS HRA, at a Community Medicaid Office, or by mail. In 2026 she qualifies with income up to $2,474 a month, and her savings do not count.

Q: My dad lives in Rochester and has $60,000 saved. Can he still get the Medicare Savings Program?
A: Yes, if his income is under the limit. New York has no resource test for QMB or QI. He applies through the Monroe County Department of Social Services.

Q: Is there an asset limit for the Medicare Savings Program in New York?
A: No. The state's income and resource chart lists no resource test for QMB or QI.

Q: Does the Medicare Savings Program give me Extra Help too?
A: Yes. Medicare says people in a Medicare Savings Program also get Extra Help, and HRA says they qualify for it automatically.

Q: What happened to SLMB in New York?
A: The state's current MSP page lists only QMB and QI. New York's QMB income limit reaches 138% of the poverty level. If you see SLMB mentioned, apply anyway and the state will check which program fits.

Q: When does the Medicare Savings Program start?
A: In New York City, HRA says QMB starts the first day of the month after you are found eligible, and QI takes effect the month you apply.

Sources: 

## How New York taxes retirement income

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/ny-retirement-income-tax/
Updated: 2026-11-25

New York is gentle on retirees. Social Security is not taxed, New York and federal government pensions are fully exempt, and most people 59½ or older can exclude up to $20,000 of other pension and IRA income. Here is how each piece works, plus a refundable credit for low-income households and where to get free help.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Does New York State tax my dad's pension if he retired from a city job in Queens?
A: No. Pensions from New York State and local government plans, including New York City retirement systems, are fully exempt from New York income tax at any age, with no dollar limit.

Q: My mom in Buffalo takes money from her IRA. Is it taxed by New York?
A: If she is 59½ or older, up to $20,000 a year of IRA withdrawals can be excluded from New York tax. Money from contributions she made after retiring does not count, and any amount above $20,000 is taxable.

Q: Does New York tax Social Security?
A: No. Social Security benefits included in federal adjusted gross income are subtracted on the New York return, so they are not taxed by the state.

Q: Can a married couple exclude $40,000 of pension income in New York?
A: Yes, if each spouse is 59½ or older and each has at least $20,000 of their own qualifying pension, annuity or IRA income. One spouse cannot use the other's unused exclusion.

Q: Are federal and military pensions taxed in New York?
A: No. Pensions from federal government plans, including the military, are fully exempt from New York income tax, separate from the $20,000 exclusion.

Q: Who can get the New York real property tax credit?
A: For tax year 2025, full-year New York residents with federal adjusted gross income of $18,000 or less who lived in the same home for six months, owning property worth $85,000 or less or paying rent of $450 a month or less. It is worth up to $375 if someone in the household is 65 or older.

Sources: 

## SCRIE and DRIE: how the NYC rent freeze works for older adults

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/scrie-drie-nyc/
Updated: 2026-11-25

New York City can freeze the rent of tenants 62 and older, and of tenants with disabilities, in rent-regulated apartments. The income limit just rose to $75,000. Here is how it works and how to sign up.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: What is the income limit for SCRIE now?
A: The Rent Freeze Program home page says the household income threshold has increased from $50,000 to $75,000. Finance told the City Council the state budget authorized the higher limit beginning July 1, 2026.

Q: How do I get my mom's rent frozen in the Bronx?
A: If she is 62 or older, lives in a rent-stabilized or rent-controlled apartment, has household income of $75,000 or less and pays more than one-third of her income in rent, apply for SCRIE online through NYC TAP or on paper. Call 311 with questions.

Q: My dad lives in a Mitchell-Lama building in Harlem. Where does he apply for SCRIE?
A: SCRIE in Mitchell-Lama and HDFC buildings is handled by HPD at 100 Gold Street, Room 7M, or 212-863-8494. DRIE applicants in those buildings apply with the Department of Finance.

Q: What is the difference between SCRIE and DRIE?
A: SCRIE is for tenants 62 and older. DRIE is for tenants 18 and older who receive SSI, SSDI, a VA disability pension or compensation, or disability-related Medicaid after past SSI or SSDI.

Q: How often do I renew SCRIE?
A: Every one or two years, depending on your benefit period. Finance mails a renewal about 60 days before the benefit ends, and you can renew online in NYC TAP.

Q: What is the SCRIE phone number?
A: Call 311. From outside New York City, or using TTY or relay, call 212-639-9675.

Sources: 

## Westchester senior exemption limits by town and city

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/senior-exemption-westchester-county-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Every Westchester city and town sets its own senior exemption limit and deadline. Here are the figures, forms and assessor phone numbers in one table.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get my mom the senior property tax exemption in Yonkers?
A: Call the Yonkers assessor at 914-377-6200 and ask for the current income limit and deadline, because Yonkers runs on its own assessment calendar. First-time applicants use Form RP-467 and renewals use Form RP-467-Rnw. Bring proof of her age and her federal tax return.

Q: When is the senior exemption deadline for my dad's house in New Rochelle?
A: Official sources differ, so call the city assessor at 914-654-2052 before you rely on a date. The Westchester County assessment calendar lists December 1 as New Rochelle's taxable status date, while the city code says May 1. The code gives a 50% exemption to income under $50,000 and a sliding scale up to $58,399.99.

Q: What is the income limit for the senior exemption in Greenburgh?
A: The Greenburgh assessor's page says gross income from all sources must be below $58,400, and applications are due May 1 each year. The exemption must be renewed every year. Call 914-989-1520 for the full scale and your parent's school district limit.

Q: Is the Westchester County senior exemption limit the same as my town's?
A: Not always. The county's 2025 senior guide lists a county limit of $58,400, and the town and city schedules posted here top out at $58,399.99, but some school districts and Peekskill's city tax still use less than $37,400. Each line of the tax bill can have its own limit.

Q: Can my parents get the senior exemption and Enhanced STAR together?
A: Yes. The state Tax Department says senior exemption recipients may also be eligible for STAR, including Enhanced STAR. Enhanced STAR has its own limit of $113,550 for 2027 benefits and only lowers school taxes.

Q: Do I have to reapply for the senior exemption every year in Westchester?
A: Many places require it. The Town of Rye and Greenburgh say you must renew every year using Form RP-467-Rnw. Ask your assessor how often your community requires a renewal, and watch the mail in winter.

Sources: 

## The senior citizens homeowners' exemption in New York and NYC

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/senior-homeowners-exemption-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

New York lets towns, cities, counties and school districts cut the taxable value of a senior's home by up to half. In New York City the program is called SCHE. Here is how the income scale works and how to apply.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: What is the income limit for SCHE in NYC?
A: Combined income of all owners and spouses cannot be more than $58,399. Income up to $50,000 gets the full 50% reduction, and the reduction shrinks in steps down to 5% between $57,500 and $58,399.

Q: How do I get my mom the senior property tax exemption in Staten Island?
A: Apply for SCHE with the NYC Department of Finance online or on paper between September 28 and March 15. All owners must be 65 or older (one is enough for spouses or siblings) and she must have owned the home for 12 months.

Q: Where does my dad in Albany County file for the senior citizens exemption?
A: He files Form RP-467 with his town or city assessor, usually by March 1. Ask the assessor what income limit the town, county and school district use, since each sets its own.

Q: How often do I renew SCHE?
A: Every two years. Finance sends a notice when renewal is due, and the renewal must be filed by March 15. DHE must be renewed every year.

Q: Does the senior exemption include Enhanced STAR?
A: No. They are separate programs. A parent who already gets Basic STAR is upgraded to Enhanced STAR automatically when eligible, but the senior exemption is its own application, filed with the assessor or, in New York City, with Finance as SCHE.

Q: Can I get both SCHE and the Disabled Homeowners' Exemption?
A: No. In New York City you cannot receive both. If you qualify for both, Finance gives you SCHE.

Sources: 

## SNAP for New Yorkers 60 and older: income limits and how to apply

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/snap-ny-seniors/
Updated: 2026-11-25

A New Yorker 60 or older living alone can have gross income up to $2,660 a month and still qualify for SNAP. Here are the current limits, the rules that help older adults, and how to apply in New York City and the rest of the state.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I help my mom apply for SNAP in Brooklyn?
A: Apply online through ACCESS HRA at nyc.gov/accesshra, or in person or by mail. You can act as her authorized representative. After applying, call the DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399 (press 2) to do the interview, because HRA will not call to schedule it.

Q: Can my dad in Rochester get SNAP if he has savings?
A: Probably yes. If his household's gross income is under New York's chart for older adults ($2,660 a month for one person through September 2027), most households face no savings test. Apply through myBenefits.ny.gov or the Monroe County Department of Social Services.

Q: What is the SNAP income limit for a senior living alone in New York?
A: For October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027, a one-person household with a member 60 or older can have gross income up to $2,660 a month ($31,920 a year). Above that, the household may still qualify by passing the net income test of $1,330 a month.

Q: What happened to NYSNIP?
A: NYSNIP was phased out in 2024, with cases switched over by November 30, 2024. It was replaced by NYSCAP, which automatically enrolls single SSI recipients that Social Security codes as living alone. Report rent, utility and medical costs to your local office so the benefit is recalculated under regular SNAP rules.

Q: Can seniors deduct medical expenses for SNAP in New York?
A: Yes. If you are 60 or older or disabled, verified out-of-pocket medical costs above $35 a month can be deducted, which raises the benefit. Premiums, prescriptions, dental bills, hearing aids and rides to medical visits can count.

Q: How do older adults get farmers market coupons in New York?
A: Low-income New Yorkers 60 and older can get a $25 coupon booklet each season starting July 1. Outside NYC, contact your county Office for the Aging or call 800-342-9871. In NYC, call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469.

Sources: 

## Social Security in 2027: what changes for New Yorkers

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/social-security-2027-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

Social Security and SSI checks rise 3.6% for 2027. Here is what that means for the average retiree, the new work limits, SSI and the New York State Supplement, the Medicare premium that comes out first, and how to reach a Social Security office in New York.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How much will my mom's Social Security go up in January 2027?
A: Benefits rise 3.6%. On a $1,900 check that is about $68 more before Medicare. Her exact amount, and what Medicare takes out, will be in her COLA notice, available online in her my Social Security account.

Q: Where is the Social Security office for my dad in Staten Island?
A: Enter his ZIP code in SSA's office locator at ssa.gov/locator to get the address, phone and hours of the office that serves him. You can also call 1-800-772-1213 to set up an appointment.

Q: What is the 2027 SSI amount in New York?
A: The federal SSI rate for 2027 is $1,029 a month for one person and $1,544 for a couple. New York adds a State Supplement. In 2026 that was $87 a month for a person living alone and $104 for a couple living alone.

Q: How much can I earn in 2027 and still collect Social Security?
A: If you are under full retirement age all year, the 2027 limit is $25,560. In the year you reach full retirement age, it is $67,920, counting only earnings before the month you reach it. After that, earnings no longer reduce benefits.

Q: What is the Medicare Part B premium in 2027?
A: The standard Part B premium for 2027 is $209.40 a month, up $6.50 from $202.90. The Part B deductible is $292.

Q: When do SSI payments go up?
A: The 3.6% raise for SSI starts with the payment on December 31, 2026. Social Security retirement and disability checks go up starting with benefits payable in January 2027.

Sources: 

## Basic and Enhanced STAR in New York: limits, rules and how to apply

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/star-enhanced-star-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

STAR cuts school taxes for New York homeowners, and the Enhanced version gives more to owners 65 and older. Here is who qualifies, what changed with the credit, and how to sign up.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: What is the Enhanced STAR income limit for 2027?
A: The limit is $113,550 for 2027 benefits and $110,750 for 2026 benefits. The state uses federal adjusted gross income minus the taxable part of IRA distributions, for owners and resident spouses only.

Q: Does my mom in Buffalo need to apply for Enhanced STAR when she turns 65?
A: In most cases, no. Since 2026 the Tax Department upgrades eligible owners to Enhanced STAR automatically in the year a resident owner turns 65, whether she gets the STAR credit or the exemption. If her check or school tax bill does not change, call her assessor or 518-457-2036.

Q: How do I sign up my dad in Brooklyn for STAR?
A: NYC Finance no longer handles STAR. Register him for the STAR credit with the state through the Homeowner Benefit Portal in an Individual Online Services account, or call 518-457-2036.

Q: Do both owners have to be 65 for Enhanced STAR?
A: No. The Tax Department says only one resident owner must be at least 65 as of December 31 of the benefit year, however the owners are related.

Q: Can I switch back to the STAR exemption after taking the credit?
A: No. Once you switch to the STAR credit, you cannot switch back to the exemption.

Q: What is the STAR phone number?
A: The Tax Department's STAR line is 518-457-2036, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Sources: 

## Utility help and shutoff protections for older New Yorkers

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/utility-help-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

New York law gives older, blind and disabled utility customers extra protection from gas and electric shutoffs, with more from November 1 to April 15. Here is how those rules work, how to register medical equipment, and where to get help with the bill.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Can the utility shut off my mom's heat in the winter in Westchester?
A: It can, but only after strict steps. From November 1 to April 15, the utility must try to reach an adult at home three days before and on the day of a heat shutoff. If harm might result, it must notify Social Services and wait 15 more business days. If everyone in the home is 62 or older, blind or disabled, more protections apply.

Q: How do I stop my dad's electric from being shut off in Queens? He's on oxygen.
A: Register his oxygen concentrator with Con Edison right away by calling 1-877-582-6633 or using the life-support form in My Account. A doctor, nurse practitioner, physician assistant or board of health official must certify it within 30 days. If a shutoff is near, call the PSC hotline at 800-342-3355.

Q: What is the medical emergency rule for utilities in New York?
A: If a doctor or the local Board of Health tells the utility that losing service would worsen a medical emergency, the utility must keep service on for 30 days. A written certificate must follow within five business days. It can be renewed if the doctor explains the need and you show you cannot pay.

Q: Do seniors have to pay a utility deposit in New York?
A: Under HEFPA, a utility cannot require a deposit from a customer 62 or older, unless service was shut off for nonpayment within the past six months. Customers on public assistance or SSI also cannot be required to pay a deposit.

Q: What is the Energy Affordability Program?
A: EAP is a monthly discount on electric and gas bills from New York's large utilities. Households on HEAP, SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, a Veterans Disability or Survivors Pension or Lifeline qualify, and since January 2026 so do households below median income. Some people are enrolled automatically, so ask your utility to check.

Q: How do I file a complaint against a utility in New York?
A: Call the utility first and write down who you spoke with. If that fails, call the Department of Public Service helpline at 800-342-3377, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., or file online. For a shutoff due within 48 to 72 hours, call the hotline at 800-342-3355.

Sources: 

## Benefits for older veterans and surviving spouses in New York

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/veterans-benefits-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Older veterans and their surviving spouses in New York can get a VA pension, extra money for care at home, a property tax break, a bed in a state veterans home and burial in a veterans cemetery. Free advisors will file the paperwork with you.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get my dad Aid and Attendance in Westchester?
A: Call the Westchester County Veterans Service Agency at 914-813-5145 or NYS Veterans' Services at 1-888-838-7697 for a free advisor. He must qualify for the VA pension (wartime service, age 65 or disabled, limited income and net worth), and a doctor must complete VA Form 21-2680 showing he needs help with daily activities.

Q: My mom is a veteran's widow in Queens. What can she get?
A: She may qualify for the VA Survivors Pension if she did not remarry and meets the income and net worth limits. If the home is in her name and she lives there, she can keep the alternative veterans property tax exemption. She can also be buried with her husband in a national cemetery. NYC Veteran Resource Centers and DVS advisors help free.

Q: How much is the VA Aid and Attendance pension?
A: The VA pays the gap between your counted income and a yearly limit. For rates in effect from December 1, 2025, the Aid and Attendance limit is $29,093 for a veteran with no dependents and $34,488 with one dependent. Unreimbursed medical costs above 5% of the limit lower counted income. The rates usually change each December.

Q: Is the veterans property tax exemption automatic in New York?
A: No. You must file Form RP-458-a with your assessor, usually by March 1, or apply with the NYC Department of Finance by March 15. You only file once unless you move or the disability rating changes. Each town, county and school district decides whether to offer it.

Q: Who can live in a New York State veterans home?
A: The homes take veterans and their spouses who need skilled nursing care, and in some cases veterans' parents and un-remarried surviving spouses. The Long Island home requires New York residency at entry into service or for a year before applying, an honorable discharge and at least 30 days of active service.

Q: Can my mom be buried with my dad in a national cemetery in New York?
A: Yes. The VA says a spouse or surviving spouse of an eligible veteran can be buried in a VA national cemetery, even if she remarried after he died. Calverton, Saratoga, Bath and Western New York have open space; Long Island, St. Albans and Woodlawn take cremated remains only.

Sources: 

## Adult day care in New York: social programs vs adult day health

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/adult-day-care-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Adult day care lets your parent spend the day somewhere safe and social, then sleep at home. New York has two very different kinds. Here is how they differ, who pays and how to find one.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I find adult day care for my mom with dementia in Staten Island?
A: Search NYC Aging's social adult day care search tool for registered programs on Staten Island, and read NYC Aging's guide to choosing one. Ask how staff handle participants with dementia. If she has a Medicaid managed long term care plan, ask the care manager which social or adult day health programs are in the network.

Q: Will Medicaid pay for adult day care for my dad in Nassau County?
A: If he is in a Medicaid managed long term care plan, adult day health care is a covered service, and social day care can be provided as a care management service. The plan must authorize it. If he is not on Medicaid, call NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871 or the Nassau County Office for the Aging about funded programs.

Q: What is the difference between social adult day care and adult day health care?
A: Social adult day gives supervision, socialization, meals and limited personal care under NYSOFA standards. Adult day health care is regulated by the Department of Health and adds nursing, therapy, pharmacy and other health services, with sessions of at least five hours.

Q: Does Medicare pay for adult day care?
A: Medicare.gov lists adult day health care as long-term care and says Medicare doesn't pay for long-term care, so families should not count on Medicare to pay for a day program. Medicaid plans, PACE, Office for the Aging funding or private pay are the usual routes.

Q: Who qualifies for a social adult day program in New York?
A: NYSOFA says a person is eligible if they need help from another person with at least one daily activity, such as toileting, mobility, transferring or eating, or need supervision because of cognitive or psychosocial impairment.

Q: How do I complain about a social adult day care in NYC?
A: Submit a comment or complaint to NYC Aging online or call 311. Every registered program must post a sign with the contact for NYC Aging's SADC Ombuds Office and a sign listing participants' rights.

Sources: 

## Assisted living in New York: licenses, costs and how to check

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/assisted-living-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

In New York, the license on the wall decides who a residence can admit and whether your parent can stay as needs grow. Here is what each license means, who pays and how to check a place before you sign.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I find assisted living for my mom in Westchester that can handle dementia?
A: Search NYS Health Profiles: Adult Care Facilities by county (Westchester) and by the service Special Needs Assisted Living Residence. A residence needs SNALR certification to serve people with dementia. Then compare rent, services and quality measures on the DOH Assisted Living Residence Quality site, and tour.

Q: Will Medicaid pay for assisted living for my dad in Queens?
A: Medicaid's main route is the Assisted Living Program (ALP). If he medically qualifies for a nursing home, an ALP in a participating adult home or enriched housing program can provide nursing, therapy, personal care and other services. Ask HRA about Medicaid in New York City. Residents on SSI also get a higher SSI amount in adult care facilities.

Q: What is the difference between an ALR and an EALR in New York?
A: A basic Assisted Living Residence gives daily food service, 24-hour on-site monitoring, case management and an individualized service plan. An Enhanced ALR can also admit or keep residents who chronically need help walking or using stairs, depend on medical equipment that needs frequent help from medical staff, or have chronic unmanaged incontinence.

Q: Does Medicare pay for assisted living?
A: No. Medicare.gov says Medicare and most health insurance, including Medigap, don't pay for long-term care, and it lists assisted living as one place where that non-medical care happens. Medicaid or private long-term care insurance may help.

Q: How can I check inspections or complaints about an assisted living residence?
A: Look up the facility on NYS Health Profiles: Adult Care Facilities, and check the DOH Assisted Living Residence Quality page for confirmed complaints, staffing, food citations and the residency agreement. To report a problem, call the DOH complaint line at 1-866-893-6772 or the Long Term Care Ombudsman Program at 1-855-582-6769.

Q: Is independent senior housing the same as assisted living?
A: No. A 2016 DOH letter says independent senior housing is not licensed by DOH. The housing provider may hand residents a list of outside agencies but cannot provide, arrange or coordinate personal care. A building that offers services like 24-hour supervision, personal care or medication management generally needs a DOH license.

Sources: 

## CDPAP in New York: how family caregivers get paid in 2026

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/cdpap-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

The Consumer Directed Personal Assistance Program lets a New Yorker on Medicaid choose their own home care aide, often an adult child or other relative. Since 2025 every case runs through one statewide payroll company. Here is how it works now.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Can I get paid to take care of my mom in Brooklyn?
A: Possibly, through CDPAP, if your mom has New York Medicaid and is assessed as needing home care. Adult children can be hired as personal assistants. In NYC, Medicaid goes through HRA. Request the home care assessment through the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350, or through her Medicaid plan.

Q: Can my dad hire me as his aide in Rochester if my mother is his wife?
A: Yes, you can be hired, but your mother cannot, because spouses are excluded. The designated representative also cannot be the paid assistant. Your dad needs Medicaid and an assessment showing he needs home care.

Q: Can a spouse be paid through CDPAP in New York?
A: No. DOH lists the consumer's spouse, the designated representative and the parent of a consumer under 21 as people who cannot be hired as personal assistants.

Q: What is PPL in CDPAP?
A: Public Partnerships LLC is New York's Statewide Fiscal Intermediary for CDPAP. All CDPAP recipients must work with PPL. It processes payroll for personal assistants and offers them a benefits package. Call 1-833-247-5346.

Q: Does my parent qualify for CDPAP with dementia?
A: For assessments on or after September 1, 2025, an adult with a dementia or Alzheimer's diagnosis must need at least supervision with more than one activity of daily living, and must meet the other CDPAP rules, including Medicaid eligibility. If they cannot direct their own care, a designated representative must do it for them.

Q: Do we have to pay to register with PPL?
A: No. DOH says there is no cost to register with PPL, and you will not be asked for bank account or credit card details over the phone.

Sources: 

## Hearing aids, glasses and dental care for older New Yorkers

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/hearing-vision-dental-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Original Medicare pays for almost none of the hearing aids, glasses and dental work older adults need. New York Medicaid covers much more, Medicare Advantage plans vary, and dental school clinics can bring the cost down.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Does Medicare pay for hearing aids for my mom in Brooklyn?
A: Original Medicare does not pay for hearing aids or the exams to fit them. It does cover a hearing test her doctor orders. New York Medicaid lists hearing aids among its benefits, and some Medicare Advantage plans add hearing coverage, so call her plan. OTC hearing aids are another option for mild to moderate loss.

Q: Where can my dad get affordable dentures on Long Island?
A: If he has New York Medicaid, dentures are covered, and replacement dentures no longer need a physician's letter. The Stony Brook School of Dental Medicine Dental Care Center takes new adult patients at 631-632-8989, prompt 4, and says its care is typically significantly more affordable than private practice.

Q: Does Medicare cover glasses after cataract surgery?
A: Yes. Part B covers one pair of eyeglasses with standard frames, or one set of contact lenses, after cataract surgery that implants a lens. You pay 20% of the Medicare-approved amount after the Part B deductible, plus any cost for upgraded frames, and the supplier must participate in Medicare.

Q: Does New York Medicaid cover dental implants?
A: In certain circumstances, yes. The Department of Health lists implants, crowns and root canals among covered services when medically necessary, and says replacement dentures and implants no longer need a letter from a physician since January 31, 2024. The dentist sends a prior approval request.

Q: Does EPIC help pay for glasses or hearing aids in New York?
A: EPIC is New York's prescription drug program for people 65 and older. The Department of Health says it gives secondary coverage for Medicare Part D and EPIC-covered drugs, and it lists eyeglasses among items EPIC does not cover. For glasses, hearing aids and dental care, check Medicaid, a Medicare Advantage plan or the VA.

Q: Who should not buy an over-the-counter hearing aid?
A: The FDA says OTC aids are for adults with perceived mild to moderate loss. See a doctor first for ear pain, fluid from the ear, heavy earwax, dizziness, sudden or fluctuating hearing change, or loss or ringing in only one ear. Someone who cannot hear speech in a quiet room should see a hearing professional.

Sources: 

## Home care agencies in New York: how to choose and check them

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/home-care-agencies-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

Before a stranger comes into your parent's home, it helps to know which kind of agency you are dealing with, who is paying and how to check them. A plain guide to LHCSAs, CHHAs, private aides and the state tools that let you verify them.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I find a licensed home care agency for my dad in Westchester?
A: Search the NYS DOH Home Health and Hospice Profiles site by county and agency type. It shows CHHAs and LHCSAs, inspection information and, for certified agencies, quality measures. Then confirm the agency's registration and ask the questions in this guide.

Q: Will Medicare pay for an aide for my mom in the Bronx after her hospital stay?
A: Medicare covers home health aide care only while she also gets skilled care, such as nursing or therapy, is homebound and has a provider's order. It does not cover 24-hour care or personal care alone. For ongoing help, look at Medicaid home care or private pay.

Q: What is a LHCSA in New York?
A: A Licensed Home Care Services Agency offers home care services, mostly to people who pay privately or have private insurance. It can also serve Medicare or Medicaid patients under contract with another provider. Since January 1, 2019, it must be registered with the Department of Health to operate.

Q: How do I check if a home health aide is certified in New York?
A: Search the NYS Home Care Registry by name or registry number. It lists aides who finished state-approved training. DOH warns that some entries may be outdated, so also check references.

Q: Where do I report a bad home care agency in New York?
A: Call the DOH Home Health Hotline at 1-800-628-5972 (staffed 8:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. weekdays), email HomeHospiceCCIP@health.ny.gov, or write to the address on the complaints page of the DOH Profiles site.

Q: Do New York home care aides get background checks?
A: State law requires home care agencies to request a criminal history check through DOH for covered prospective employees. Ask the agency to confirm the check was completed. Families hiring privately must check references themselves.

Sources: 

## Hospice care in New York: who qualifies, costs and choosing one

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/hospice-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

What the Medicare hospice benefit covers, what it costs, where care happens and how to check a New York hospice before you call it.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get hospice for my mom at home in Queens?
A: Ask her doctor whether she qualifies, then search Medicare Care Compare and the NYS Hospice Profiles site for hospices approved to serve Queens. Call two or three, ask about visit frequency and night coverage, and have her doctor send the referral. Medicare pays for covered hospice care at $0.

Q: Does Medicare pay for my dad's nursing home room in Westchester if he goes on hospice?
A: No. Medicare hospice pays for the hospice care, drugs for pain and symptoms and equipment, but not room and board in a nursing home. That charge is paid by savings, long-term care insurance or Medicaid if he qualifies.

Q: What happens if my parent lives longer than six months on hospice?
A: Hospice can continue. After two 90-day periods, Medicare allows an unlimited number of 60-day periods. A hospice doctor or nurse practitioner meets with your parent and the hospice recertifies that they are still terminally ill.

Q: Can my parent leave hospice?
A: Yes. Medicare says a person always has the right to stop hospice at any time, for example to try a new treatment. They can go back to hospice later if they still qualify.

Q: What is the difference between hospice and palliative care?
A: Palliative care relieves symptoms at any stage of a serious illness and can be given alongside curative treatment. Hospice is palliative care for people who are terminally ill and have chosen comfort care instead of a cure.

Q: Who do I call with a complaint about a hospice in New York?
A: Call the Department of Health Home Health Hotline at 1-800-628-5972, which takes calls 24 hours a day, or email HomeHospiceCCIP@health.ny.gov. Staff answer the phone weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.

Sources: 

## Managed long term care in New York: MLTC, NYIA and plan choice

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/managed-long-term-care-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

If your parent has Medicare and Medicaid and needs ongoing help at home, a managed long term care plan is usually how that help arrives. Here is how the assessment, plan choice and switching rules work in New York.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get my mom home care through Medicaid in the Bronx?
A: She needs Medicaid through HRA first. Then call the New York Independent Assessor at 855-222-8350 (TTY 1-888-329-1541) to schedule the nurse assessment and clinical appointment. If she qualifies and has Medicare too, she enrolls in a plan through New York Medicaid Choice at 1-888-401-6582, and the plan's care manager sets her home care plan.

Q: Can my dad in Orange County switch his MLTC plan if the aide keeps missing shifts?
A: In the first 90 days after enrolling he can switch for any reason. During the following nine-month lock-in he needs good cause, and a plan failing to provide appropriate care under the plan of care counts. Call New York Medicaid Choice at 1-888-401-6582, and ICAN at 1-844-614-8800 can help.

Q: Who has to join a managed long term care plan in New York?
A: DOH says enrollment in an MLTC partial capitation plan is mandatory for people with both Medicare and Medicaid, age 21 or older, who need community based long-term services for more than 120 days, meet the minimum needs test and live in New York State.

Q: What is the difference between MLTC, MAP and PACE?
A: An MLTC partial capitation plan covers long-term care like home care, while Medicare and regular Medicaid cover doctors, hospitals and drugs. Medicaid Advantage Plus puts all Medicare, Medicaid, long-term care and drug benefits under one organization. PACE, for people 55 and older, covers primary, acute and long-term care through one team.

Q: Does an MLTC plan cover CDPAP?
A: Yes. DOH lists Consumer Directed Personal Assistance Services among the services MLTC plans cover when medically necessary. The plan authorizes the hours.

Q: What happens to the MLTC plan if my parent moves into a nursing home?
A: DOH says MLTC partial capitation plans cover only three months of long-term nursing home care. If the stay goes past three months, New York Medicaid Choice sends a letter saying when your parent will leave the plan.

Sources: 

## How to compare Medicare Advantage plans in New York

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/medicare-advantage-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

A Medicare Advantage plan replaces Original Medicare with one private plan, usually with a network and drug coverage built in. In New York the choice is less of a one-way door than elsewhere, because Medigap can be bought any time of year. Here is how to compare plans for your parent.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Should my mom in Rockland County switch to Medicare Advantage?
A: It depends on her doctors, drugs and health. Medicare Advantage usually has a network and may need prior approval, but it caps yearly costs. Because New York insurers must sell Medigap any time of year, she can return to Original Medicare later more easily than in most states. Call HIICAP at 1-800-701-0501 to compare.

Q: How do I find a Medicare Advantage plan that my dad's doctors in Queens take?
A: Search each plan's provider directory on Medicare Plan Finder or the plan's website, then call every doctor's office and ask whether it takes that exact plan for next year. HIICAP counselors at 1-800-701-0501 can help you compare plans free.

Q: Can I switch from Medicare Advantage back to Original Medicare in New York?
A: Yes. You can switch during Open Enrollment (October 15 to December 7) or the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period (January 1 to March 31). New York insurers must accept a Medigap application any time, though a pre-existing condition wait of up to six months may apply, shortened by prior coverage.

Q: What is a D-SNP in New York?
A: A Dual Eligible Special Needs Plan is a Medicare Advantage plan for people who have both Medicare and Medicaid. It coordinates both sets of benefits and includes doctor, hospital and drug coverage. In New York, Medicaid Advantage Plus (MAP) pairs a D-SNP with long-term care for people who need home care or similar services.

Q: Does EPIC work with Medicare Advantage?
A: Yes, if the Medicare Advantage plan includes Part D drug coverage. Part D pays first, then EPIC gives secondary coverage for approved drugs. EPIC members also get a chance once a calendar year to join a drug plan or a Medicare Advantage plan with drug coverage. The EPIC Helpline is 1-800-332-3742.

Q: What do Medicare star ratings mean?
A: Medicare uses star ratings from 1 to 5 to compare plans on quality and performance. If a 5-star plan is offered in your area, you can switch to it once between December 8 and November 30. A plan rated under 3 stars for the last 3 years lets members switch any time.

Sources: 

## Medicare costs in 2027 for New Yorkers

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/medicare-costs-2027-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

Every main 2027 Medicare premium, deductible and coinsurance figure from CMS, in plain English, plus the New York programs (Medicare Savings Program, Extra Help and EPIC) that can lower the bill.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How much is the Medicare Part B premium in 2027?
A: The standard Part B premium is $209.40 a month in 2027, up from $202.90 in 2026. The yearly Part B deductible is $292. People with income above $112,000 (single) or $224,000 (joint) pay more under IRMAA.

Q: How do I get help paying my mom's Medicare premium in Queens?
A: Apply for New York's Medicare Savings Program, which has no resource test. In New York City you can get help at an HRA Medicaid office (HRA Helpline 1-888-692-6113). For free help with the form, call HIICAP NYC at 212-341-3978 or Aging Connect at 212-244-6469.

Q: What is the Part A deductible for 2027?
A: The Part A inpatient hospital deductible is $1,776 per benefit period in 2027. It covers your share of the first 60 days. Days 61 to 90 cost $444 a day, and skilled nursing days 21 to 100 cost $222 a day.

Q: What is the most my dad in Albany will pay for prescriptions in 2027?
A: With a Part D plan, his out-of-pocket costs for covered drugs are capped at $2,400 for 2027. After that he pays $0 for covered drugs for the rest of the year, though his plan premium is a separate cost. If his income is modest, Extra Help or New York's EPIC program can lower costs further. HIICAP (1-800-701-0501) can check both for free.

Q: What does Part A cost if you do not have 40 work quarters?
A: In 2027 Part A costs $328 a month with 30 to 39 quarters of work and $597 a month with fewer than 30. A spouse's work record can count. New York's QMB program can pay the Part A premium for people who qualify by income.

Q: Can I appeal a high IRMAA charge?
A: Yes. If income dropped because of retirement, marriage, divorce, a spouse's death or similar events, file form SSA-44 with Social Security. You can submit it online, by mail or fax, or call 1-800-772-1213.

Sources: 

## Medicare open enrollment and changing plans in New York

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/medicare-open-enrollment-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

The dates that matter, what you can change in each window, how to compare plans on Medicare.gov, and where New York families get free help before December 7.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: When is Medicare open enrollment for 2027 coverage?
A: Open enrollment runs from October 15 to December 7, 2026, and changes start January 1, 2027. People in Medicare Advantage get one more change from January 1 to March 31, 2027.

Q: How do I help my dad pick a Medicare drug plan in Buffalo?
A: List his drugs, doses and pharmacy, then enter them in the Medicare Plan Finder at medicare.gov and sort by total estimated cost. For a free walk-through, call HIICAP at 1-800-701-0501 and say you are in Erie County to reach the local counselors.

Q: Someone called my mom in Brooklyn offering a better Medicare plan. Is it real?
A: Be careful. NYSOFA says plans are not allowed to call people to market a plan. Do not give out her Medicare number. Call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) or HIICAP NYC at 212-341-3978 to check her options.

Q: Can I leave Medicare Advantage and go back to Original Medicare?
A: Yes, during open enrollment (October 15 to December 7) or the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period (January 1 to March 31). In New York, Medigap insurers must accept you any time, though a waiting period of up to six months for pre-existing conditions may apply.

Q: What is HIICAP?
A: HIICAP is New York's free Medicare counseling program, with counselors based in local offices for the aging. Call 1-800-701-0501, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and say your county.

Q: Can I change plans if I move or go into a nursing home?
A: Yes. Moving out of your plan's area opens a Special Enrollment Period, and so does living in or leaving a nursing home. In the nursing home case, the window lasts while your parent lives there and for two full months after the month they move out.

Sources: 

## Medigap in New York: buy any time, same price at any age

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/medigap-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

New York lets older adults buy a Medicare Supplement policy any month of the year at a community-rated price. Here is how it works, what is sold and how to compare.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Can you buy a Medigap plan any time in New York?
A: Yes. New York law requires insurers selling Medigap to accept a Medicare enrollee's application at any time of year, and they cannot deny you or charge more because of your health. A pre-existing condition waiting period of up to six months may apply.

Q: Does Medigap cost more as you get older in New York?
A: No. New York requires Medigap to be community rated, meaning premiums are set without regard to age, sex, health status, tobacco use or occupation. Prices vary by insurer and by region.

Q: How do I find a Medigap plan for my mom in Westchester?
A: Enter her ZIP code in the DFS Medicare Supplement Rate Look-up to see every insurer's monthly rate, then compare the same plan letter across companies. HIICAP (1-800-701-0501) can go over the choices with you for free.

Q: My dad in Rochester has a health condition. Can he switch from Medicare Advantage to Medigap?
A: Yes. He can leave Medicare Advantage during open enrollment (October 15 to December 7) or January 1 to March 31, and a New York Medigap insurer must accept him. The policy may have a waiting period of up to six months for pre-existing conditions, shortened by prior coverage with no break over 63 days.

Q: Can I still buy Medigap Plan F in New York?
A: Only if you first became eligible for Medicare before January 1, 2020. Plans C, F and F+ are closed to people who became eligible on or after that date.

Q: Does Medigap cover prescription drugs?
A: No. Medigap policies sold after 2005 do not include drug coverage, so you need a separate Part D plan. In New York, EPIC can add help on top of Part D for people 65 and older.

Sources: 

## Memory care in New York: dementia housing, costs and help

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/memory-care-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

New York has no license called memory care. Here is what the real options are for a parent with dementia, what they cost by region, where Medicaid helps and the free state programs that support families.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I find memory care for my dad in Rockland County?
A: Search NYS Health Profiles: Adult Care Facilities for Rockland County and the service Special Needs Assisted Living Residence. A residence needs SNALR certification to serve people with dementia. For nursing homes, see our nursing home ratings guide and ask each home how it cares for residents with dementia.

Q: Will Medicaid pay for my mom's memory care in Brooklyn?
A: Medicaid can pay for home care, CDPAP and adult day health care through a managed long term care plan, for services in a participating Assisted Living Program, and for long-term nursing home care if she qualifies. DOH says people who can no longer pay privately for a SNALR generally have to turn to Medicaid, which often means a move to a nursing home. The SNALR voucher program was created to prevent that. Ask HRA about Medicaid in Brooklyn.

Q: What is a SNALR in New York?
A: A Special Needs Assisted Living Residence is an assisted living residence with a DOH certificate to serve people with special needs, most commonly Alzheimer's disease or other dementia. It must have a special needs plan showing how residents' needs will be safely met.

Q: How much does memory care cost in New York?
A: DOH's SNALR voucher eligibility document, last updated June 2021, listed average monthly SNALR costs from $5,800 in Northeastern New York to $10,602 in New York City. Prices have likely changed, so get written rates from each residence.

Q: Who qualifies for the SNALR voucher program?
A: DOH lists a dementia diagnosis, at least 12 months at the current facility in a participating SNALR, income and assets under regional limits, no large transfers in the year before applying, and not being on Medicaid or SSI. Up to 200 vouchers may be issued, and a waitlist may apply.

Q: Where can I get free help caring for a parent with dementia in New York?
A: DOH funds Centers of Excellence for Alzheimer's Disease, Alzheimer's Association community programs with a 24-hour helpline at 1-800-272-3900, and regional caregiver support programs with respite. NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871 links you to local services in your county.

Sources: 

## Nursing home ratings in New York: stars, inspections, staffing

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/nursing-home-ratings-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

How Medicare's five-star ratings work, where to find New York inspection and staffing records, how nursing home bills get paid and who to call when something goes wrong.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I check a nursing home's inspection record for my mom in Buffalo?
A: Look the home up on Medicare Care Compare and open the Inspections tab, then search the NYS Nursing Home Profiles site (profiles.health.ny.gov) by Erie County. Profiles shows state inspection results, complaints and enforcement actions. Focus on citations where residents were harmed and on problems that repeat.

Q: My dad is in rehab at a nursing home in Brooklyn after a hospital stay. How long will Medicare pay?
A: Medicare Part A covers up to 100 days of skilled nursing or rehab per benefit period if he had at least 3 inpatient days in a row first and still needs daily skilled care. Days 1 to 20 cost $0 a day once the Part A deductible ($1,776 in 2027) is paid. Days 21 to 100 cost $222 a day in 2027. Coverage stops sooner if he no longer needs skilled care.

Q: What is the minimum staffing a New York nursing home must have?
A: State law requires at least 3.5 hours of care per resident per day from certified nurse aides, licensed practical nurses and registered nurses. At least 2.2 of those hours must come from aides and at least 1.1 from licensed nurses.

Q: What does a yellow warning sign on Care Compare mean?
A: It means the home is in the federal Special Focus Facility program for homes with a history of serious quality problems. These homes are inspected at least every six months and do not get star ratings while in the program.

Q: How much money can my parent keep after Medicaid starts paying for a nursing home?
A: A Medicaid resident in a New York nursing home keeps $50 a month as a personal needs allowance. Most other income goes toward the cost of care. Ask your county Department of Social Services, or HRA in New York City, about the rules for a spouse still living at home.

Q: Who do I call to complain about a nursing home in New York?
A: Call the DOH Nursing Home Complaint Hotline at 1-888-201-4563 or use the online complaint form. For help advocating for a resident, call the Long Term Care Ombudsman Program at 1-855-582-6769. If someone is in danger, call 911 first.

Sources: 

## NY Connects: where New Yorkers start for long-term care help

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/ny-connects/
Updated: 2026-11-25

One free phone number links your family to home care, meals, transportation and help applying for Medicaid. Here is what NY Connects does, how it works in New York City and upstate, and how to get the most out of the first call.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: What is the NY Connects phone number?
A: Call 1-800-342-9871. The statewide line connects you to the NY Connects office for the county where the person needing help lives. In New York City, you can also call the borough partner directly.

Q: How do I get home care help for my mom in Queens?
A: Call NY Connects in Queens, run by Selfhelp Community Services for NYC Aging, at 718-559-4400, or the statewide line at 1-800-342-9871. If she has Medicaid and needs personal care, the assessment is scheduled through the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350.

Q: My dad lives in Buffalo and I live in Manhattan. Who do I call?
A: Call 1-800-342-9871 and ask for the NY Connects office that serves Erie County, where your dad lives. Services are arranged by the older adult's address, so the Manhattan office will send you to his county.

Q: Does NY Connects cost anything?
A: No. NY Connects is free and unbiased information and assistance. Some services it refers you to may have costs or eligibility rules, and the specialist can explain those.

Q: Does my parent have to be on Medicaid to use NY Connects?
A: No. NY Connects serves people regardless of how they pay, privately, through public programs or both. It can also help you find out if your parent could qualify for Medicaid and help with the application.

Q: Is NY Connects only for older adults?
A: No. It serves older adults and people with disabilities of all ages, plus their families, caregivers and the professionals who help them.

Sources: 

## PACE in New York: all-in-one care for older adults at home

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/pace-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

PACE, a Medicare and Medicaid program, gives one team responsibility for nearly all of your parent's care, so they can stay at home instead of moving to a nursing home. It runs only in certain counties. Here is how it works in New York.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Is there a PACE program for my mom in Brooklyn?
A: Yes. The DOH plan directory lists Centerlight Healthcare PACE in Kings County (Brooklyn). Call the program to confirm it serves her address and to set up an intake visit.

Q: Can my dad join PACE in Rochester?
A: The DOH directory lists ElderONE for Monroe County, which includes Rochester. He must be 55 or older, need a nursing home level of care and be able to live safely at home with PACE's help.

Q: How much does PACE cost with Medicaid in New York?
A: Medicare.gov says people with Medicaid pay no monthly PACE premium, and there is no deductible, copay or coinsurance for care and drugs the PACE team approves.

Q: Can someone with only Medicare join PACE?
A: Medicare.gov says people with Medicare but not Medicaid pay a monthly premium for the long-term care portion and a premium for Part D drugs. Ask the New York PACE program in your area how enrollment works without Medicaid.

Q: Does PACE include prescription drugs?
A: Yes. PACE covers prescription drugs, and for people with Medicare it provides Part D coverage. Joining a separate Medicare drug plan will disenroll your parent from PACE.

Q: Does my parent have to go to a nursing home to use PACE?
A: No. PACE is for people who need a nursing home level of care but can live safely at home with PACE's help. PACE covers nursing home care only when it is medically necessary.

Sources: 

## Elder abuse and Adult Protective Services in New York

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/adult-protective-services-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

If you think an older New Yorker is being hurt, neglected or cheated, you can make a report today. Here is who to call in New York City and the rest of the state, and what happens next.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I report that my mom is being taken advantage of in the Bronx?
A: Call NYC Adult Protective Services at 718-557-1399, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., call 311, or refer online at nyc.gov/apsrefer. If money was stolen, also call the police. If she is in danger right now, call 911.

Q: Who do I call about my dad being neglected by a caregiver in Syracuse?
A: Call Onondaga County's Adult Protective Services unit, or the state APS helpline at 1-844-697-3505, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 8 p.m. If he is in immediate danger, call 911.

Q: Can I report elder abuse anonymously in New York?
A: Yes. New York City APS accepts anonymous referrals and keeps the information confidential. Outside the city, county APS units such as Tompkins County's keep the caller's identity confidential unless you want the person to know.

Q: Does Adult Protective Services cost money or have an income limit?
A: APS serves adults 18 and older regardless of income. Eligibility depends on having an impairment, being unable to protect themselves or manage daily needs, and having no one willing and able to help.

Q: Can APS remove my parent from their home?
A: APS works to help people stay safely at home and adults can usually refuse services. If someone cannot make decisions and is at risk, a court may appoint a guardian, which is a separate legal process.

Q: Where do I report a scam call targeting an older adult in New York?
A: Call the NY Attorney General's helpline at 1-800-771-7755 or file online at ag.ny.gov/file-complaint. You can also report to the FTC at reportfraud.ftc.gov and to the FBI at ic3.gov.

Sources: 

## Help for family caregivers in New York: respite, leave and support

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/caregiver-support-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

New York has free counseling, respite, dementia support and paid leave for people caring for an older relative. Here is where to start, who qualifies and what each program pays.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get help caring for my mom in Queens?
A: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 and say you are a family caregiver. NYC Aging will connect you with the caregiver program for your mom's community district, which can offer counseling, support groups, training, respite and benefits help.

Q: Can I get paid to take time off to care for my dad in Buffalo?
A: If you work for a private employer in New York, Paid Family Leave can pay you 67% of your average weekly wage for up to 12 weeks. The cap is $1,228.53 a week in 2026 and $1,287.91 for leave starting in 2027. Your dad can live anywhere, including out of state.

Q: Who runs caregiver support outside New York City?
A: Each county Office for the Aging runs the National Family Caregiver Support Program and other services. Call NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871 to reach the office in the county where your loved one lives.

Q: Is there help for caregivers of someone with dementia in New York?
A: Yes. The state Health Department funds regional caregiver support programs with assessments, support groups, education and respite. There is also a 24-hour Alzheimer's Association helpline at 800-272-3900.

Q: Can I take Paid Family Leave a day at a time?
A: Yes. PFL can be taken in full-day increments instead of all at once. The number of days depends on how many days a week you usually work, so a three-day-a-week worker can take up to 36 days.

Q: Does New York have a tax credit for family caregivers?
A: There is no general caregiver credit. The state child and dependent care credit can cover care for a disabled spouse or adult dependent who lived with you more than half the year. The long-term care insurance credit is 20% of qualifying premiums, up to $1,500.

## Caring for an aging parent in New York: the first 90 days

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/caring-for-aging-parent-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Your mom or dad needs more help and you are not sure where to begin. Here is who to call, the papers to sign, the benefits to check and how to weigh home care against assisted living or a nursing home.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Who do I call to get help for my aging mom in Brooklyn?
A: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469. NYC Aging can connect your mom with a local case management agency, which does a phone intake and a home visit and can arrange meals, benefits help and, if she is not on Medicaid, city-funded home care. Brooklyn's NY Connects partner, PSS, is at 718-671-6200.

Q: My dad in Westchester just got out of the hospital. What do I do first?
A: Call NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871 to reach the Westchester office for the aging, and make sure you were named as his caregiver so the hospital trains you on his care at home. Then confirm his follow-up visits and get a health care proxy and power of attorney signed if he does not have them.

Q: Does a health care proxy let me pay my parent's bills?
A: No. A New York health care proxy covers medical decisions only. For banking and bills your parent needs a power of attorney, signed before a notary and two witnesses while they still have capacity.

Q: What is MOLST and does my parent need one?
A: MOLST is New York's form for medical orders about CPR and other life-sustaining treatment. It is meant for people with serious health conditions who live in or need long-term care, or who might die within the next year. A physician, nurse practitioner or physician assistant signs it after talking with your parent.

Q: Can I take paid time off to care for my parent?
A: If you work for a covered New York employer, Paid Family Leave can pay 67% of your average weekly wage for up to 12 weeks to care for a parent with a serious health condition, even one who lives out of state. The cap is $1,287.91 a week for leave starting in 2027.

Q: When is it time for assisted living instead of home care?
A: Consider it when your parent cannot live safely on their own even with help at home, but does not need ongoing nursing care. New York's adult homes and assisted living residences are non-medical settings. If your parent needs continual nursing care, a nursing home or PACE may fit better.

Sources: 

## Dementia and Alzheimer's help for New York families

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/dementia-help-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

A parent with Alzheimer's or another dementia changes everything. Here are the state-funded programs, where they are near NYC and the Hudson Valley, and the legal, safety and care steps to take.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Where can I get help for my mom with dementia in the Bronx?
A: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 and say you are a dementia caregiver. The state's list shows Presbyterian Senior Services for the Regional Caregiver Support Initiative in the Bronx. Its caregiver program, PSS Circle of Care, is at 866-665-1713, and the Alzheimer's Association 24-hour helpline is 800-272-3900.

Q: How do I get respite for my dad with Alzheimer's in Westchester?
A: Ask the Westchester office for the aging (through NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871) about caregiver respite, and call the Alzheimer's Association Hudson Valley Chapter at 845-471-2655, which the state lists for caregiver support there. State-funded dementia respite can include overnight stays.

Q: Does Medicare pay for a dementia evaluation?
A: Yes. Medicare Part B covers a separate visit to review cognitive function, confirm a diagnosis such as dementia or Alzheimer's disease and make a care plan. After the Part B deductible, your parent pays 20% of the Medicare-approved amount.

Q: What is a Center of Excellence for Alzheimer's Disease?
A: It is one of ten regional centers funded by the state Department of Health. They diagnose and manage Alzheimer's and related dementias, refer families to community support, support primary care doctors and refer patients to research and clinical trials.

Q: Can my parent with dementia still sign a power of attorney?
A: Only if they still have capacity. New York requires a power of attorney to be signed by a principal with capacity, before a notary and two witnesses. If your parent can no longer sign, a court guardianship may be needed.

Q: What should I do if my parent with dementia wanders off?
A: Search the immediate area for no more than 15 minutes, then call 911 and tell police your parent has dementia and is a vulnerable adult. The state Missing Persons Clearinghouse supports families and runs alerts for missing vulnerable adults at risk of harm. Its hotline is 1-800-346-3543.

Sources: 

## EISEP in New York: home care for older adults not on Medicaid

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/eisep-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

The Expanded In-home Services for the Elderly Program helps New Yorkers 60 and older who need help at home but do not qualify for Medicaid. Here is who gets it, what it costs and how to apply.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get home care for my dad in Brooklyn if he is not on Medicaid?
A: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469. NYC Aging will refer him to a local case management agency, which assesses his needs and decides whether he qualifies for city-funded home care for people 60 and older who are not eligible for Medicaid home care.

Q: My mom lives in Westchester and needs help with housework. Can EISEP help?
A: Possibly. EISEP covers people 60 and older who need help with at least two household tasks, like cleaning and shopping, or one personal care task. Call NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871 to reach the Area Agency on Aging in Westchester County and request an assessment.

Q: Is there an income limit for EISEP?
A: There is no income limit to apply. Income sets the cost share. People at or below 150% of the federal poverty level pay nothing, those between 150% and 250% pay on a sliding scale, and those at or above 250% pay the full cost.

Q: Can someone on Medicaid get EISEP?
A: No. EISEP is for older adults who are not eligible for the same services through Medicaid. If your parent qualifies for Medicaid, the county will usually point you to Medicaid home care instead.

Q: How many hours of help does EISEP give?
A: It depends on the assessment and the county. In New York City, the limit is 8 hours a week for housekeeping only, and 20 hours a week for personal care plus housekeeping, with extra hours possible for special situations.

Q: What can I do if EISEP denies or ends services?
A: You have the right to a hearing on a denial, a disputed cost share or an involuntary discharge. Ask for it out loud or in writing within 30 days of receiving the notice.

Sources: 

## Elder care in Orange County, NY: home care, EISEP and who to call

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/elder-care-orange-county-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

The four ways to get help at home in Orange County, the one number that opens most doors, caregiver groups in Middletown and Newburgh, and how to check providers.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get help at home for my mom in Newburgh?
A: Call Orange County NY Connects at 845-615-3710. If she is 60 or older and does not qualify for Medicaid, ask for an EISEP referral; a case manager visits and sets up help on a sliding scale. If she has Medicaid, NY Connects refers home care to the DSS Home Care Unit, and the first assessment is booked with NYIA at 855-222-8350.

Q: My dad lives in Port Jervis and I live in New Jersey. How do I set up care from here?
A: Call NY Connects at 845-615-3710 and explain what has changed. If he is homebound, ask Aging Services Specialists at 845-615-3700 for a home visit. To book a NYIA assessment for Medicaid home care, you need to be an authorized representative on file with NYIA, or he can call himself.

Q: Can I get paid to care for my father in Middletown?
A: Possibly, through CDPAP, if he has Medicaid and a state assessment finds he needs home care. A son or daughter can be his paid personal assistant. His spouse or designated representative cannot. Start with NYIA at 855-222-8350. Payroll runs through PPL at 1-833-247-5346.

Q: Is there a caregiver support group in Orange County NY?
A: Yes. The Office for the Aging runs monthly groups in Middletown and Newburgh and a virtual group every Thursday at noon. Call the Caregiver Program at 845-862-5333, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Q: Where can I find a list of home care agencies in Orange County?
A: The Office for the Aging posts lists of certified and licensed home care agencies, hospices, nursing homes and adult homes serving the county on its Information and Assistance page. Check each one on NYS Health Profiles (or Hospice Profiles for a hospice) for inspection information before you hire. A listing is not an endorsement.

Q: Does Medicare pay for home care in Orange County?
A: Only for home health care. Medicare pays $0 for covered part-time skilled nursing or therapy when your parent is homebound and a doctor orders it, with aide visits while skilled care continues. It does not pay for 24-hour care, meal delivery or personal care when that is the only help needed.

## Elder care in Rockland County, NY: home care, CDPAP and who to call

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/elder-care-rockland-county-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

The four ways to get help at home in Rockland, the county lines for each, free respite for caregivers and how to check any agency or nursing home first.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get home care for my mom in Nyack?
A: Call Rockland NY Connects at 845-364-3444 for a free phone review of her needs. If she is 60 or older and not eligible for Medicaid, ask the Office for the Aging about EISEP at 845-364-2110. If she has Medicaid, call Rockland DSS Adult Services at 845-364-3100, option 5.2, and schedule a NYIA assessment at 855-222-8350.

Q: I live in Bergen County. Can I set up care for my dad in Spring Valley from New Jersey?
A: Yes. NY Connects, the Office for the Aging and DSS all take calls from family members out of state. For a NYIA assessment, you can call if you are an authorized representative on file with NYIA. A private care manager can also be your eyes on the ground; our Rockland County page lists practices serving the county.

Q: Can I get paid to take care of my mother in New City?
A: Possibly, through CDPAP, if she has Medicaid and a state assessment finds she needs home care. Adult children can be hired as her personal assistant. A spouse or her designated representative cannot. Start with NYIA at 855-222-8350, and payroll runs through PPL at 1-833-247-5346.

Q: Does Rockland County give family caregivers a break?
A: Yes. For residents 60 and older who have a caregiver, the Office for the Aging offers a free week-long stay at an assisted living facility or 40 hours of home health aide care. The county's flyer puts the home care option at 40 hours. It depends on availability and funding. Call 845-364-2110.

Q: How do I check if a home care agency in Rockland is licensed?
A: Search the agency on NYS Health Profiles at profiles.health.ny.gov/home_care, filtered by Rockland County. The profile shows inspection information, and certified home health agencies also show quality measures. You can also look up an individual aide on the state Home Care Registry.

Q: Does Medicare pay for an aide at home in Rockland County?
A: Only as part of home health care. Medicare pays $0 for covered part-time skilled care when your parent is homebound and a doctor orders it, and an aide can be included while skilled care continues. It does not pay for 24-hour care or for personal care when that is the only help needed.
