## Elder care in Westchester County, NY: home care, EISEP, who to call

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/elder-care-westchester-county-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

The four ways to get help at home in Westchester, the right DSS line for each Medicaid question, adult day programs by town and how to check providers.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get home care for my dad in Yonkers?
A: If he is 60 or older, call the Westchester EISEP case management unit at 914-813-6442 for a free home visit and care plan, with aide hours on a sliding fee. If he has Medicaid and no managed care plan, call the DSS Home Care Unit at 914-813-6612. If he is in a plan, call the plan.

Q: My mom lives in White Plains and I live in Bergen County. What is the first call?
A: Call NY Connects at 914-813-6300. Calls are confidential and you can call for her from New Jersey. If she needs hands-on help, ask for the EISEP unit at 914-813-6442, which sends a case manager to her home and includes family in the assessment where possible.

Q: Can I get paid to care for my mother in New Rochelle?
A: Possibly, through CDPAP, if she has Medicaid and a state assessment finds she needs home care. An adult child can be hired. A spouse or her designated representative cannot. Start with NYIA at 855-222-8350. Pay runs through PPL, the statewide fiscal intermediary, at 1-833-247-5346.

Q: Are there adult day programs in Westchester County?
A: Yes. The county lists six medical adult day programs in Dobbs Ferry, Ossining, Valhalla, Hawthorne, Mount Vernon and Yonkers, and five social programs in Ossining, Mount Vernon, Hartsdale and Cortlandt Manor. Phone numbers are on the county's Adult Care Services pages.

Q: Which DSS number do I call about Medicaid for a parent at home in Westchester?
A: For a new community Medicaid application, call 914-813-6147. For home care, call the Home Care Unit at 914-813-6612. For questions about the long-term care medical needs assessment, call 914-995-6214. The DSS main line is 914-995-3333.

Q: How do I check a hospice or nursing home in Westchester?
A: For a hospice, use the state's Hospice Profiles at profiles.health.ny.gov/hospice, which show inspection results and the counties each hospice is licensed to serve. For a nursing home, use Nursing Home Profiles, then Medicare Care Compare, where each nursing home gets an overall rating of 1 to 5 stars. Visit in person before you decide.

## Geriatric care managers in New York: what they do and cost

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/geriatric-care-manager-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

A geriatric care manager can coordinate a parent's care when the family can't do it all. Here is what they do, what to check before you hire one and the free alternatives in New York.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I find a care manager for my mother in Westchester?
A: ALCA has a search tool for its members by ZIP code, and you should check any license on the NYS Office of the Professions lookup. Before paying, call NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871 to ask the Westchester office for the aging about free case management such as EISEP.

Q: Is there free care management for my dad in Staten Island?
A: Yes. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469. NYC Aging funds local case management agencies for residents 60 and older, and its case managers do not charge for their time. Some services they arrange may have a fee or suggested contribution based on income.

Q: Does New York license geriatric care managers?
A: Not as a separate profession. Care management is not among the licensed professions in Title VIII of the Education Law, which the Office of the Professions oversees. Many care managers hold a social work or nursing license, which you can check on the state's online lookup.

Q: Does Medicare pay for a geriatric care manager?
A: ALCA says care manager fees may not be covered by insurance, so ask your parent's plan. What Medicare Part B may pay for is chronic care management by a doctor or other provider, if your parent has two or more serious chronic conditions expected to last at least a year, with 20% coinsurance after the deductible.

Q: What does CMC mean after a care manager's name?
A: CMC stands for Care Manager Certified, a certification from the National Academy of Certified Care Managers. It is one of four certifications the Aging Life Care Association accepts for its Advanced Professional level.

Q: Should a care manager also sell home care?
A: Some practices do both. ALCA suggests asking whether the company also provides home care. If it does, ask how it makes sure its recommendations fit your parent's needs and not its own services.

Sources: 

## Article 81 guardianship in New York: when it's needed, how it works

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/guardianship-article-81-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

When a parent can no longer manage money or care decisions and never signed a power of attorney, a court may need to appoint a guardian. Here is how New York's Article 81 process works.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I become guardian for my dad in the Bronx?
A: You file an Article 81 petition in the Bronx County Supreme Court, starting with an order to show cause and verified petition. The judge sets a hearing within 28 days of signing the order and usually appoints a court evaluator. NYC residents 60 and older can get free legal help, including on guardianship, through Aging Connect at 212-244-6469.

Q: How long does an Article 81 guardianship take in New York?
A: The hearing must be held no more than 28 days after the judge signs the order to show cause. Preparing the papers beforehand, and the guardian qualifying afterward, add time. Contested cases usually take longer.

Q: Do I need guardianship if my mom in Westchester already has a power of attorney?
A: Often not. The court must consider whether existing resources such as a power of attorney and health care proxy already meet her needs. A guardian may still be needed if the documents don't cover a problem, or if she is in danger and refusing help.

Q: What are the court fees for guardianship in New York?
A: In Supreme Court, the index number is $210 and the request for judicial intervention is $95, with $45 for each motion. Lawyer, court evaluator and bond costs are separate and usually larger.

Q: When is the guardian's annual report due in New York?
A: Every guardian must file a report annually in May, unless the court orders otherwise. The initial report is due within 90 days of receiving the commission.

Q: Is there free help for family members who become guardians?
A: Yes. The New York courts' Guardian Assistance Network gives free help to family guardians statewide, including one-on-one help with required reports and online training that meets the court-ordered requirement. It does not give legal advice.

Sources: 

## Health care proxy, living will and MOLST in New York

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/health-care-proxy-molst-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

How to sign New York's health care proxy, what a living will adds, who decides when there is no proxy, and how MOLST orders work for people who are seriously ill.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get my dad to sign a health care proxy in Nassau County?
A: Print the free New York State Health Care Proxy form from health.ny.gov. He names an agent and an alternate, then signs in front of two adults who are not the agent or alternate. No lawyer or notary is needed. Give copies to his doctor and his agent.

Q: My mom is in a nursing home in the Bronx and has no proxy. Who makes medical decisions?
A: Under the Family Health Care Decisions Act, a surrogate decides. A legal guardian can decide if one has been appointed. Otherwise it is the first available person in this order: spouse or domestic partner, an adult child, a parent, an adult sibling, then a close friend. The surrogate must follow her known wishes or her best interests.

Q: Does a New York health care proxy need to be notarized?
A: No. New York's form needs only two witnesses who are 18 or older. Your agent and alternate agent cannot be witnesses.

Q: What is the difference between MOLST and a DNR?
A: A DNR order covers only CPR. MOLST (form DOH-5003) is a set of medical orders covering CPR, breathing tubes and other life-sustaining treatment. It is the only form in New York that can record both a nonhospital DNR and a DNI order.

Q: Is a photocopy of a MOLST form valid?
A: Yes. DOH says photocopies, faxes, scans and other accurate copies of a signed MOLST are valid. It does not have to be on pink paper. Stamped signatures are not allowed.

Q: Can I cancel or change my health care proxy?
A: Yes. Tell your agent or your health care provider, out loud or in writing. Then sign a new form and give out new copies. If you named your spouse and later divorce or legally separate, they can no longer be your agent unless you said otherwise on the form.

Sources: 

## Long-distance caregiving for a parent in New York

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/long-distance-caregiving-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Your parent lives in New York and you live in New Jersey or farther away. Here is how to set up local help, the permissions you need, money and mail, telehealth and an emergency plan.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get help for my mom in Rockland County if I live in New Jersey?
A: Call NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871 and ask for the Rockland County office for the aging. Explain that you live out of state and ask for one named contact. Rockland also has one of the state's Caregiver Resource Centers, and caregivers do not need to live with the person they help to use it.

Q: My dad lives in Queens and I live in Bergen County. Who do I call?
A: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469. NYC Aging can connect your dad with a local case management agency that visits his home. Queens' NY Connects partner, Selfhelp Community Services, is at 718-559-4400.

Q: Can I sign as agent on my parent's power of attorney on a different day?
A: Under New York law your parent's signature and your signature as agent are each acknowledged before a notary. The law says a gap in time between the two acknowledgments does not by itself make the power of attorney invalid.

Q: Can I join my parent's doctor visit by video?
A: Yes, if the doctor offers telehealth. Medicare covers telehealth from anywhere in the U.S., including home, through December 31, 2027. Your parent pays 20% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible, usually the same as in person.

Q: Does New York Paid Family Leave cover care for a parent who lives out of state?
A: Yes. If you work for a covered New York employer, you can take Paid Family Leave to care for a parent with a serious health condition, including family members outside New York State. You can take it in full-day increments.

Q: What if my parent with dementia goes missing?
A: Search the immediate area for no more than 15 minutes, then call 911 and tell police your parent has dementia and is a vulnerable adult. The state Missing Persons Clearinghouse supports families and runs alerts for vulnerable adults who are missing and at risk of harm. Its hotline is 1-800-346-3543.

Sources: 

## Power of attorney in New York: the form, the rules and the bank

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/power-of-attorney-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

A power of attorney lets someone you trust handle your money and paperwork if you can't. Here is how New York's form works since the 2021 changes, and what to do when a bank pushes back.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Does a New York power of attorney need two witnesses?
A: Yes. Since June 13, 2021, the principal's signature must be witnessed by two people who are not named as agents or gift recipients, and it must be notarized. The notary can serve as one of the two witnesses.

Q: How do I get power of attorney for my mom in Brooklyn?
A: Your mom has to sign it herself while she still has capacity. She signs the New York statutory short form before a notary and two witnesses, and you sign as agent before a notary. NYC residents 60 and older can get free legal help through Aging Connect at 212-244-6469. If she can no longer understand what she's signing, you may need an Article 81 guardianship instead.

Q: My dad's bank in Buffalo won't accept his power of attorney. What can I do?
A: Under New York law the bank must accept it, reject it in writing with reasons, or ask you for a notarized agent affidavit within 10 business days of getting the original or an attorney-certified copy. Ask for the rejection in writing, fix any real problem it names, and respond. An unreasonable refusal can lead to a court proceeding where the bank may owe damages and attorney's fees.

Q: Is a power of attorney signed before 2021 still good in New York?
A: Yes. A power of attorney that was valid when it was signed remains valid under the 2021 law. Some families update older forms anyway so banks see the current version, or because an agent has changed.

Q: Can a power of attorney make medical decisions in New York?
A: No. The New York statutory short form covers financial and legal matters only and says the agent cannot make health care decisions. Use a separate health care proxy for medical choices.

Q: Does a power of attorney still work after my parent dies?
A: No. It ends at death. After that, the executor named in the will, or an administrator appointed by the Surrogate's Court, handles the estate.

Sources: 

## Senior help where New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania meet

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/tri-state-port-jervis-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Port Jervis, Matamoras, Milford and Montague are minutes apart, but each sits in a different state. Here is which office, drug program and tax break your parent can use, side by side.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: My mom lives in Milford, PA and I'm in Bergen County. Who do I call to get her help at home?
A: Call the Pike County Area Agency on Aging at 570-775-5550 or toll free 800-233-8911, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm. It does assessments, care management, home-delivered meals and personal care aides. Your Bergen County address does not matter. Her Pennsylvania address does.

Q: My dad in Port Jervis stopped driving. How does he get to the store and appointments?
A: The City of Port Jervis Dial-A-Ride runs Monday to Friday, 6 am to 3:30 pm, within the city and up to 3 miles into Deerpark. The senior fare is 50 cents. Call 845-856-7999 between 8 am and 1 pm, by noon the business day before the ride.

Q: Can my parent in Matamoras use New York's EPIC if they fill prescriptions in Port Jervis?
A: No. EPIC requires a permanent home in New York State. A Matamoras resident would look at Pennsylvania's PACE or PACENET drug programs instead, which require being a Pennsylvania resident for at least 90 days before applying. Call 1-800-225-7223.

Q: Does Medicare cover doctors across the state line?
A: Original Medicare lets you use any doctor or hospital that takes Medicare, so the state line does not matter. Medicare Advantage and Part D plans have service areas and networks, so check the plan before booking care in another state.

Q: My aunt in Montague, NJ needs help paying for prescriptions. What program fits?
A: New Jersey's PAAD program is for state residents 65 or older, or 18 to 64 on Social Security disability. For 2026, income must be less than $54,943 single or $62,390 married. Copays are $5 for generics and $7 for brand names. Call 1-800-792-9745.

Q: Who takes elder abuse reports in Pike County, PA?
A: Pennsylvania's 24-hour Elder Abuse Helpline is 1-800-490-8505, run by the PA Department of Aging, and reports can be anonymous. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911 or local police right away.

Sources: 

## Free college classes for New Yorkers 60 and older

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/free-college-classes-seniors-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

At 60, you can sit in on real college classes at SUNY and CUNY campuses for little or nothing. Here are the rules, the fees, and how five campuses near New Jersey handle senior auditors.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Can my mom take free classes at SUNY Rockland Community College?
A: Yes, if she is 60 or older. Rockland Community College waives tuition for seniors who audit credit courses, though she pays any lab or course fees. Registrations are processed one week after the semester starts. Call Records and Registration at 845-574-4328.

Q: How does my dad audit a class at Hunter College in Manhattan?
A: He must be a New York State resident aged 60 or older. He applies online with proof of age, proof of address and proof of MMR shots, then registers on the second day of the semester. Fees are $65 plus $15 a semester. The spring priority deadline is January 15.

Q: Is college free for seniors in New York?
A: Auditing is free or nearly free. SUNY campuses charge senior auditors no tuition, and some charge small fees. Hunter and Queens charge $80 a semester in fees, and the College of Staten Island charges $65 plus its consolidated service fee. Taking a course for credit costs regular tuition.

Q: Do senior auditors get grades or credit?
A: No. Auditors attend without exams, grades or credit. Some instructors invite auditors to join discussions and some prefer that they listen, so ask on the first day.

Q: Can I audit online classes at SUNY?
A: Often, yes. SUNY Orange allows online and hybrid courses if you have your own computer and internet. SUNY Purchase's winter 2027 courses are all online, with email registration opening December 18 at 1 p.m.

Q: Are there art and writing classes for older adults at the Queens library?
A: Yes. Queens Public Library offers grant-funded Creative Aging courses such as drawing, watercolor, quilting and memoir writing. Ask the library about any cost. Call Older Adult Services at 718-464-0084 or 718-776-6800 to find one near you.

## Working after 60 in New York: job help, pay limits and your rights

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/jobs-after-60-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

New York has paid job training for low-income workers 55 and older, free Career Centers for everyone, and strong age discrimination laws. Here is how they work, and how a paycheck affects Social Security.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How can my mom in the Bronx find a part-time job at 62?
A: Call NYC Aging's Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 and ask for employment services. If she is unemployed and low income, the Older Adult Employment Program offers paid training and an internship. ReServe places city residents 50 and older in part-time roles of 10 to 20 hours a week. The Department of Labor's Career Center locator also lists free centers in the Bronx and across the city.

Q: Can my dad in Westchester get paid job training at 58?
A: Yes, if he is unemployed and his family income is no more than 125% of the federal poverty level. The Senior Community Service Employment Program (SCSEP) pays the highest of the federal, state or local minimum wage for an average of 20 hours a week. Westchester County's SCSEP page says to call a peer counselor at the Urban League of Westchester, 914-428-5850.

Q: How much can I earn on Social Security in 2027?
A: If you are under full retirement age all year, the 2027 limit is $25,560, and Social Security withholds $1 for every $2 above it. In the year you reach full retirement age, the limit is $67,920 for the months before your birthday month, with $1 withheld for every $3 above it. After that there is no limit.

Q: Can an employer in New York refuse to hire me because of my age?
A: No. The New York State Human Rights Law bans age discrimination in hiring and on the job, and it covers every employer in the state regardless of size. Report it to the Division of Human Rights at 844-697-3471 within three years. Filing is free.

Q: Will my pension reduce my unemployment benefits in New York?
A: It can. The Department of Labor says pension payments may affect your benefit amount, and you must tell it if you receive or apply for a pension. Report it when you file, and the Department will figure the effect on your claim.

Q: What is the Silver Stars program?
A: Silver Stars, run by NYC Aging, offers part-time, temporary work at City agencies to fully retired New York City employees who receive a City pension. Participants keep collecting their pension. Search "silver" on the NYC Careers job site, or email silverstars@aging.nyc.gov.

## Older drivers in New York: renewal, vision tests and the keys talk

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/older-drivers-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

New York never ends a license because of age. Here is how renewal and the vision test work, how a family member can ask the DMV to review a driver, and how to plan for life after driving.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I report my dad's unsafe driving to the DMV in Westchester?
A: Fill out DMV form DS-7, Request for Driver Review, with specific incidents, dates and places, sign it, and mail the original to Medical Review Unit, NYS DMV, 6 Empire State Plaza, Room 337, Albany, NY 12228. The DMV does not take reports by phone or email, and your name and signature are required.

Q: Does my mom in Staten Island need a road test to renew her license?
A: No. New York has no age-based road test. She needs to pass a vision test, with at least 20/40 in one or both eyes, with or without glasses. She can test at a DMV office or with a Vision Registry provider, then renew online, by mail or in person.

Q: At what age do you have to stop driving in New York?
A: There is no set age. The DMV says it will not remove driving privileges based on age or any standard except driving ability. A driver can be re-evaluated when the DMV gets a specific report from a doctor, police officer or someone who knows the driver.

Q: How much is the defensive driving discount in New York?
A: Completing a DMV-approved Point and Insurance Reduction Program course reduces the base rate of auto insurance premiums by 10% each year for three years. Take it once every 36 months to keep the discount. Only the principal operator on a policy gets the reduction.

Q: Will the DMV tell my parent who reported them?
A: The DS-7 form requires your name, signature and relationship to the driver, and the DMV may contact you. At the interview, the examiner explains the information that was received and lets the driver respond. Ask the DMV about confidentiality before you file.

Q: What can my parent use as ID after giving up driving?
A: A New York State non-driver photo ID. The DMV lets drivers exchange a current license, or one that expired within the last two years, for a non-driver ID by mail or at a DMV office. It provides the same proof of identification as a driver license.

Sources: 

## Senior centers in New York: meals, classes and how to find one

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/senior-centers-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Anyone 60 or older in New York can join a senior center for lunch, classes and company, with no income test. Here is what centers offer, what meals cost and how to find one in your county or borough.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I find a senior center for my mom in Queens?
A: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 or 311, or use the NYC Aging service finder online and enter her address. Older adult center membership is free for New Yorkers 60 and older. Ask the center for its monthly calendar and whether it serves breakfast, dinner or grab-and-go meals.

Q: Is there a senior lunch program near my dad in Rockland County?
A: Yes. The Rockland County Office for the Aging lists congregate meal providers including Meals on Wheels Programs and Services of Rockland in Nanuet (845-624-6325) and the Martin Luther King Multi Purpose Center in Spring Valley (845-425-8910). Call ahead to register and ask about lunch days.

Q: Do you have to pay for lunch at a New York senior center?
A: No. NYSOFA says there is no charge for congregate meals. You are offered a chance to make a suggested voluntary contribution, such as $3.50 in Erie County or $3 in St. Lawrence County. Contributions are confidential and no one can be denied a meal for not giving.

Q: Can my spouse come to a senior center if they are under 60?
A: Yes, for meals. NYSOFA says a spouse can get meals at a community dining site even if they are under 60. A person with a disability under 60 who lives with an older adult may use the site too. Some counties, such as St. Lawrence, charge a guest fee to other people under 60.

Q: Do I need a reservation to eat at a senior meal site?
A: Often, yes. Erie County requires advance reservations, Westchester County requires pre-registration, and St. Lawrence County asks for 24 hours' notice. Call the site or your county Office for the Aging before the first visit.

Q: What if my parent can't get to a senior center?
A: Ask about rides, since some sites provide transportation. If your parent can't prepare meals, they may qualify for home-delivered meals after an interview with the county Office for the Aging or NYC Aging. Call NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871 to start.

Sources: 

## Access-A-Ride in NYC: how to qualify, book and pay

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/access-a-ride-nyc/
Updated: 2026-11-25

Access-A-Ride is the MTA's shared-ride service for New Yorkers whose disability keeps them off buses and subways. Here is how to apply, book a trip and pay, plus what's available outside the city.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I sign my mom up for Access-A-Ride in Queens?
A: Start with the MTA's online inquiry form (aar.mta.info/inquiry) or call 877-337-2017 and choose option 4. The MTA mails an application and an appointment for a free in-person assessment, with free round-trip transportation. A decision comes within 21 days of the assessment.

Q: Does my dad in Staten Island qualify for Access-A-Ride just because he's over 65?
A: No. Access-A-Ride is based on disability, and age alone doesn't qualify anyone. He qualifies if a disability keeps him from using buses and subways some or all of the time. At 65 he does qualify for MTA reduced fare, which is a separate program.

Q: How much is an Access-A-Ride trip?
A: The fare matches the full subway and bus fare, $3. A personal care attendant listed on the AAR ID rides free. Guests pay the full fare in exact change.

Q: Can I book Access-A-Ride for the same day?
A: No. Trips are booked one to two days in advance, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., by calling 877-337-2017 (option 2) or through MY AAR or the MTA app.

Q: Does Access-A-Ride go to Long Island or Westchester?
A: Only a short way. The service area includes a three-quarter-mile band beyond the city line into nearby parts of Nassau and Westchester. Beyond that, local paratransit applies, such as NICE Able-Ride in Nassau (516-228-4000) or SCAT in Suffolk (631-853-8337).

Q: How do I cancel an Access-A-Ride trip?
A: Cancel at least two hours before pickup through MY AAR or the MTA app, or call 877-337-2017. Choose option 2 for trips booked 1 to 2 days out (7 a.m. to 5 p.m.) or option 3 for a trip today (24/7).

Sources: 

## New York estate tax: the 2026 exclusion, the cliff and filing

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/estate-tax-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

Most New York estates owe no state estate tax, but the ones near the line need to plan carefully. Here is the 2026 exclusion amount, the cliff, and what an executor must file.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: What is the New York estate tax exemption for 2026?
A: The basic exclusion amount is $7,350,000 for dates of death from January 1 through December 31, 2026. For 2025 deaths it was $7,160,000.

Q: What is the 2027 New York estate tax exclusion?
A: As of late November 2026, the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance had not published the 2027 amount. Check tax.ny.gov for the update.

Q: Will my parents' house in Nassau County push their estate over the New York limit?
A: Add the house's value to their bank and retirement accounts, life insurance they own and other assets. If the total for a 2026 death is more than $7,350,000, the estate must file Form ET-706. Above $7,717,500 (105% of the exclusion), tax applies to the whole taxable estate.

Q: My dad lived in Florida but owned a cabin in the Adirondacks. Does his estate owe New York tax?
A: A nonresident's estate must file if it includes New York real estate or tangible property and the federal gross estate plus includible gifts is more than the exclusion amount. The Form ET-706 instructions explain how a nonresident estate's tax is figured, so ask the estate's accountant to work through them.

Q: When is the New York estate tax return due?
A: Form ET-706, along with a completed federal Form 706, and any tax due must be filed and paid within nine months of the date of death. Extensions are requested on Form ET-133.

Q: Can my mom give money away to avoid New York estate tax?
A: Taxable gifts made within three years of death are generally added back to a New York resident's estate. Gifts made earlier are not added back, so planning ahead matters. Talk to an estate planning lawyer before making large gifts.

Sources: 

## Funeral and burial costs in New York: your rights and the help

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/funeral-burial-costs-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

A funeral is one of the biggest purchases a family makes, usually in a day or two and in grief. Here is what New York and federal law say you're owed, how prepaid plans work, and where help with the bill comes from.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get help paying for my mom's funeral in the Bronx?
A: If she was a low-income city resident without money or assets to cover the funeral, apply to HRA's Office of Burial Services within 120 days of her death. It pays up to $1,700, and the total bill generally has to be $3,400 or less after certain costs are subtracted. Call 718-557-1399 for help.

Q: Can my dad prepay his funeral if he's applying for Medicaid in Westchester?
A: Yes. New York requires a prepaid funeral agreement for a Medicaid applicant to be irrevocable. It then doesn't count as a resource, and paying fair market value isn't treated as a transfer. He may also keep a separate burial fund of up to $1,500 in some cases. Leftover money goes to the county.

Q: Do I have to buy the casket from the funeral home?
A: No. Under the FTC Funeral Rule and New York rules, you can buy a casket or urn online or from a local seller. The funeral home must accept it and can't charge a handling fee.

Q: Is embalming required in New York?
A: No. State law doesn't require it, and the funeral director needs your approval to embalm. A funeral home may require it for some choices, such as an open-casket viewing. Direct burial and direct cremation don't need it.

Q: How much does the VA pay toward a veteran's funeral?
A: For a death on or after October 1, 2026, VA lists $1,032 for burial and $1,032 for a plot when the veteran met one of its conditions, such as getting a VA pension or dying in VA care. Its highest rate, for some deaths on or after September 11, 2001, is up to $2,000. Burial in a VA national cemetery is free for eligible veterans.

Q: Can I get my money back from a prepaid funeral in New York?
A: If the agreement is revocable, yes, with interest and no fees or penalties. If it's irrevocable, which is required for Medicaid and SSI applicants, the money can't be refunded, but it can be moved to another funeral home.

Sources: 

## Home safety changes in New York: grab bars, ramps and repair help

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/home-modifications-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Grab bars, ramps and urgent repairs can keep a parent safely at home. Here are the New York programs that help pay, who qualifies, and the low-cost changes that prevent falls.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get grab bars installed for my mom in Queens?
A: Call NYC Aging's Older Adult Home Modification Program at 212-602-4455 or email HomeMod@aging.nyc.gov. For eligible older adults, a licensed occupational therapist assesses the home and a licensed contractor installs changes such as grab bars, handrails and shower chairs at no cost.

Q: Is there help paying for a wheelchair ramp for my dad in Westchester?
A: Possibly, through New York's Access to Home program, for people with a documented disability and household income at or below 80% of area median income. Check HCR's list of active local grants by county for a Westchester administrator, and call the county Department of Senior Programs and Services.

Q: Who qualifies for the RESTORE program in New York?
A: Homeowners 60 and older who live in the home as their primary residence and have household income at or below 100% of the area median income. The repair must fix an emergency or code violation that threatens health or safety. Apply through a local program administrator, not HCR.

Q: Can renters get accessibility modifications in New York?
A: Yes. Access to Home can assist rental units, as long as the landlord isn't already required by law to make the changes. Renters can also apply for free weatherization. In NYC, the NYC Aging Home Modification Program serves eligible older adults.

Q: Does weatherization cost anything for seniors in New York?
A: No. HCR says there is no cost to eligible homeowners and renters. Households at or below 60% of state median income may qualify, seniors get priority, and anyone receiving SSI, public assistance or HEAP is automatically eligible. Owners of rental buildings pay part of the cost.

Q: What are the cheapest ways to prevent falls at home?
A: The NYS Department of Health suggests clearing clutter from stairs and walkways, removing or taping down throw rugs, using non-slip mats in the tub, improving lighting, keeping everyday items within reach, and installing grab bars and stair handrails. It also recommends yearly eye exams and a medicine review.

Sources: 

## Moving a parent between New Jersey and New York: what changes

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/moving-parent-nj-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Lots of families straddle the Hudson. When a parent moves from Bergen County to Rockland, or from Queens to Hackensack, some things move with them and some have to start over. Here is the list.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: My mom has Medicaid in Bergen County. If she moves in with me in Rockland County, does it transfer?
A: No. Medicaid is run by each state, so she has to apply in New York once she lives here. New York can't make her wait a set period first. Apply through the Rockland County Department of Social Services, and tell New Jersey the moving date so her case closes.

Q: We're moving Dad from Staten Island to New Jersey. How long does he have to get a NJ license?
A: New Jersey's Motor Vehicle Commission says he must transfer his out-of-state license within 60 days of the move or before the current license expires, whichever comes first. The car's title and registration also have to move within 60 days.

Q: Can my parent keep a Medicare Advantage plan after moving from New Jersey to New York?
A: Only if the plan serves the new address. If not, Medicare gives a Special Enrollment Period to switch. It runs from the month of the move (or the month before, if the plan was told first) through 2 full months after.

Q: How soon must a new New York resident get a New York license?
A: Within 30 days of becoming a resident, in person at a DMV office. New York treats living in the state for 90 days as presumed residency.

Q: Does New Jersey have an estate tax?
A: Not for deaths on or after January 1, 2018. New Jersey still has an inheritance tax, but spouses, children, grandchildren, parents and stepchildren are Class A beneficiaries and exempt. New York has an estate tax with a 2026 exclusion of $7,350,000.

Q: Does Enhanced STAR follow a parent who moves to New York?
A: No. STAR belongs to the home. A new homeowner registers for the STAR credit. For Enhanced STAR, one resident owner must be 65 by December 31 of the benefit year, with income of $113,550 or less for 2027 benefits.

Sources: 

## Moving a parent between New York and Pennsylvania: what changes

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/moving-parent-ny-pa/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Medicare moves with your parent. EPIC, STAR, Medicaid and the driver's license do not. Here is how New York and Pennsylvania compare, with each state's own figures and the aging office for each NJ-near PA county.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: My mom is moving from Rockland County to Milford, PA. When does she lose EPIC and get PACE?
A: EPIC is for people whose permanent home is in New York, so it ends once Milford becomes her permanent home. PACE and PACENET need 90 days of Pennsylvania residency before she applies. Keep her Part D plan, or switch it during the moving Special Enrollment Period if it does not serve Pike County. Call PACE at 1-800-225-7223.

Q: My dad in Staten Island is moving near us in Bucks County. Can he keep his Medicare Advantage plan?
A: Only if the plan serves Bucks County. If it does not, Medicare gives him a Special Enrollment Period that starts the month he moves (or the month before, if he tells the plan first) and lasts two full months after. The Bucks County Area Agency on Aging, 267-880-5700, offers free Medicare counseling through PA MEDI.

Q: Does Pennsylvania tax my parent's pension and Social Security?
A: Pennsylvania's tax guide lists Social Security and distributions from eligible Pennsylvania retirement plans after retirement age as never taxable. Early IRA withdrawals can be taxable. Check how the specific plan is treated, since federal qualified status does not decide it.

Q: Will my parent's New York Medicaid home care continue after a move to Pennsylvania?
A: No. Medicaid does not transfer between states. Your parent applies in Pennsylvania through COMPASS, by phone at 1-866-550-4355 or at the County Assistance Office. Pennsylvania has no minimum time as a resident for Medicaid.

Q: If Dad moves to Pennsylvania but keeps his house in Westchester, does New York estate tax still matter?
A: It can. Tax.ny.gov says a nonresident's estate may have to file a New York estate tax return if it includes real or tangible property in New York and is over the basic exclusion amount, which is $7,350,000 for 2026 deaths. Pennsylvania inheritance tax may also apply. Ask an estate attorney.

Q: How soon does my mother need a Pennsylvania driver's license?
A: PennDOT says within 60 days of becoming a resident. She fills out Form DL-180R, brings proof of identity and residency and her Social Security card, passes a vision test and surrenders her New York license.

Sources: 

## Probate in New York: Surrogate's Court steps, fees and timing

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/probate-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

When a parent dies in New York, their property usually passes through the Surrogate's Court. Here is which proceeding you need, what to file, what the court charges and how long creditors have.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Do I have to probate my mom's will in Queens if she only had a bank account?
A: It depends on the account. If the account named a beneficiary or was joint with survivorship, it may pass outside probate. If it was in her name alone and worth $50,000 or less, and she owned no real estate in her name alone, you can likely use the small estate process in Queens County Surrogate's Court for a $1 filing fee.

Q: How do I handle my dad's estate in Albany if he had no will?
A: File a petition for letters of administration in the Albany County Surrogate's Court, naming all distributees and attaching a certified death certificate and a copy of the paid funeral bill. If his personal property was $50,000 or less and he owned no real estate in his name alone, the small estate process may apply instead.

Q: What is the small estate limit in New York?
A: Personal property with a gross value of $50,000 or less, not counting certain property set aside for the family under state law. Real estate in the decedent's name alone takes the estate out of the small estate process.

Q: How much does probate cost in New York?
A: The court's filing fee ranges from $45 for estates under $10,000 to $1,250 for estates of $500,000 or more. A small estate costs $1 to file. Lawyer fees, bonds and certified copies are extra.

Q: How long do creditors have to file claims against a New York estate?
A: Generally 7 months from the date letters are first issued to an executor or administrator. A fiduciary who pays lawful claims and distributions in good faith before a late claim arrives is not personally liable for those payments.

Q: Can I file probate papers online in New York?
A: In some counties, yes, through NYSCEF, the New York State Courts Electronic Filing system. Check the courts' e-filing county list or call your county's Surrogate's Court.

Sources: 

## MTA reduced fare for 65+: half-price subway, bus and train rides

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/reduced-fare-mta-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-25

At 65, New Yorkers can ride MTA subways and local buses for half price and get up to half off on the commuter railroads. Here is how to get the Reduced-Fare OMNY card, and what other New York transit systems offer.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get my dad a senior MetroCard in Manhattan?
A: The MTA now issues a Reduced-Fare OMNY card instead. Take him to an MTA Customer Service Center or the office at 3 Stone Street in Lower Manhattan with a valid photo ID. Riders 65 and older can often get the card the same day.

Q: How much is the subway for seniors in NYC?
A: Riders 65 and older pay $1.50 on subways and local buses, half the $3 base fare. After 12 paid rides in seven days on a Reduced-Fare OMNY card, the rest of that week's rides are free.

Q: Can my mom in Westchester use her Medicare card for a discount on Metro-North?
A: Yes. A Medicare card is one of the IDs Metro-North accepts for a reduced-fare ticket, which is half the one-way peak fare. Reduced-fare tickets can't be used on weekday trains arriving at Grand Central between 6 and 10 a.m.

Q: How long does it take to get a Reduced-Fare OMNY card by mail?
A: The MTA says new mail applicants may wait up to three months. Applying in person is faster, and riders 65 and older can often get the card the same day.

Q: Can I apply for MTA reduced fare online?
A: Not right now. The MTA says the online application is not available. Apply in person at a Customer Service Center or Mobile Sales van, or by mail to MTA New York City Transit, Attn: Reduced Fare Program, 130 Livingston St, Brooklyn, NY 11201-9625.

Q: Do seniors get a discount on LIRR?
A: Yes. Riders 65 and older pay half the one-way peak fare. The discount isn't valid on weekday morning peak trains arriving at Penn Station, Grand Central, Atlantic Terminal, Hunterspoint Avenue or Long Island City between 6 and 10 a.m.

Sources: 

## Scams aimed at older New Yorkers and where to report them

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/scams-older-adults-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Most scams aimed at older adults follow the same script: a familiar name, an emergency, a rush and a strange way to pay. Here is how the common ones work in New York and exactly who to call.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: My dad in Queens got a call saying his grandson was in jail and needed bail. What do I do?
A: Have him hang up and call the grandson or another relative directly on a number he knows. If he already paid, call his bank right away, then file a police report and report it to the NY Attorney General at 1-800-771-7755. If someone is coming to the house for cash, call 911.

Q: How do I report that my mom in Westchester was scammed out of money?
A: Call her bank first to see if the payment can be stopped. Then file a police report, report to the NY Attorney General at 1-800-771-7755 and to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. If someone she knows is taking her money, call Westchester County's Department of Social Services for Adult Protective Services.

Q: Does Social Security ever call and threaten arrest?
A: No. The Social Security Inspector General says Social Security will never threaten arrest unless you pay right away, suspend your number, or ask for gift cards, wires, internet currency or mailed cash. Report these calls at oig.ssa.gov.

Q: Will my utility call and shut off power today unless I pay?
A: The NYS Department of Public Service says real utilities send several mailed disconnection notices first and don't demand payment only by gift card, crypto, wire or payment app. Hang up and call the utility on a number you know is real, such as the one on your bill.

Q: Who do I call about Medicare fraud?
A: Call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227). For a Medicare Advantage or drug plan, you can also call I-MEDIC at 1-877-772-3379. Medicare says it never calls to sell anything or visits homes.

Q: Can the bank get back money sent to a scammer?
A: Sometimes, if you act fast. Call the bank or card company right away and ask them to stop or reverse the payment. Cryptocurrency payments usually can't be reversed, according to the FTC.

Sources: 

## Senior fares on New York trains, ferries and county buses

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/senior-fares-trains-ferries-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Half fares start at 60, 62 or 65 depending on the system, and each one has its own ID and rush-hour rules. Here is what Metro-North, the LIRR, the ferries, the county buses and NJ TRANSIT actually charge older riders.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: Can my mom ride the bus for free in Rockland County?
A: Right now, yes. Rockland County says fare collection is waived and Transport of Rockland (TOR) and TRIPS rides are free at this time. When fares return, the TOR senior fare is $1 for riders 60 and older with proof of age. Call 845-364-3333 for current details.

Q: How does my dad in Westchester get the senior fare on the Bee-Line?
A: He pays $1.50 if he is at least 65, or holds a Medicare card and shows photo ID. He can pay cash with a Half-Fare ID card or tap a personalized Reduced-Fare OMNY card, which caps his weekly cost at $17.50. Bee-Line no longer takes MetroCard. Call 914-813-7777 for help.

Q: Can I use my Medicare card for a discount on the LIRR or Metro-North?
A: Yes. A Medicare card is one of the IDs both railroads accept for a reduced-fare ticket, which is half the one-way peak fare. A Medicaid card is not accepted. The ticket can't be used on weekday morning peak trains arriving at the city terminals between 6 and 10 a.m.

Q: Is the Staten Island Ferry free for seniors?
A: It's free for everyone. NYC DOT runs it between St. George and Whitehall every day of the year, and you don't need a ticket or senior ID.

Q: How do seniors get the NYC Ferry discount?
A: Riders 65 and older apply to the Ferry Discount Program online or by mail with proof of age, such as a Medicare card or government ID. Processing takes up to 30 days. Once approved, buy discount one-way tickets in the NYC Ferry app or at the Wall Street/Pier 11 landing. NYC Ferry's ticketing page listed them at $1.50 in November 2026.

Q: Does NJ TRANSIT give a senior discount to New York residents?
A: Yes. Riders 62 and older save 50% or more on the regular one-way fare on NJ TRANSIT trains, buses and light rail at any time, and you don't need to live in New Jersey. On trips to or from Metro-North stations, Metro-North's rules apply and the age is 65.

## Affordable senior housing in New York: how to apply and where

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/senior-housing-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Low-cost senior apartments in New York come with income limits and long waiting lists. Here is how Section 202, NYCHA, Section 8, Housing Connect and state-financed housing work, and how to get on the lists.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get my mom on a waiting list for senior housing in Brooklyn?
A: Apply to several programs at once. File a NYCHA public housing application online at selfserve.nycha.info (or call 718-707-7771 for a paper one), register on NYC Housing Connect and apply to lotteries with 62+ set-asides, and contact Section 202 buildings in Brooklyn directly. Each list is separate.

Q: How can my dad find low-income senior apartments in Westchester?
A: Search HousingSearch.ny.gov for HCR-financed properties, call the county's Section 8 administrator (CVR New York Westchester HCVP, applicant inquiries 914-873-1045) when its list is open, and ask the Westchester Department of Senior Programs and Services and local housing authorities for senior building lists.

Q: How long is the wait for NYCHA senior housing?
A: NYCHA says it cannot estimate when you will be called because the waitlist is very large and vacancies are low. Applicants who live or work in New York City are prioritized. Keep the application current and renew it every two years.

Q: What is the income limit for Section 202 senior housing?
A: Section 202 is for very low-income households, and HUD says household income must be less than 50% of the area median income where the property is. The dollar limit depends on the county and household size, and rent is typically 30% of adjusted income. Ask the property's manager for its current limits.

Q: Is a 55+ community the same as assisted living in New York?
A: No. A 55+ community is regular housing that meets federal age rules, such as at least 80% of units having an occupant 55 or older. Adult homes and assisted living are licensed by the state, overseen by the Department of Health, and provide meals, personal care and supervision.

Q: Can I apply for both NYCHA public housing and Section 8?
A: Yes. NYCHA lets you apply for both, but you can only receive one at a time. If you are selected for one, your priority on the other list is significantly reduced. HCR's Section 8 lists are separate and require their own application.

Sources: 

## Senior transportation in Orange County, NY: every ride, town by town

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/senior-transportation-orange-county-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Orange County has no single senior bus. It has Dial-A-Ride in eleven towns, villages and cities, a few free or donation senior buses, three local bus systems and a train into New Jersey. Here is what serves each town and what it costs.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How can my mom in Warwick get to her doctor if she stops driving?
A: The Town of Warwick Dial-A-Ride picks up curb to curb on weekdays for $1.00 for riders 60 and older, disabled riders and Medicare card holders, with exact change. Call 845-986-2877 between 8 am and 2 pm, at least 24 hours and up to a week ahead. The bus also runs set-day trips to Middletown medical centers and Monroe. If she has Medicaid, Medical Answering Services (866-932-7740) arranges free rides to medical visits.

Q: Is there a senior bus for my dad in Washingtonville?
A: Yes. The Blooming Grove Senior Bus serves residents over 60 in the Town of Blooming Grove, including Washingtonville and South Blooming Grove. It picks up at home and goes to doctors and shopping on set days of the week. Call 845-496-4411 at least 24 hours ahead. A $1 donation each way is requested.

Q: What is the senior fare on Dial-A-Ride in Orange County?
A: It depends on the town: $0.50 in Montgomery and Crawford, Highlands, the Town of Newburgh and Port Jervis; $1.00 in Monroe, Wallkill and Warwick; $2.00 in Goshen and Chester; and, for riders 65 and older in Kiryas Joel, $1.50 inside the village and $3.00 outside it.

Q: Who can use Transit Orange ADA Paratransit?
A: People whose disability keeps them from using the local bus for some or all trips. You must apply and get an ADA Paratransit ID card from Orange County; call 845-615-3850. Rides cost $0.75 one way and must start and end within three quarters of a mile of a local bus route.

Q: Does my parent in Middletown have a door-to-door ride?
A: Yes. The City of Middletown Senior Shuttle gives door-to-door rides to city residents 60 and older, weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm and Sundays 8 am to 12:30 pm, for a $1 suggested donation. Call 845-346-4070. The city's local buses charge seniors $0.75.

Q: What does the Port Jervis Line cost for seniors?
A: Riders 65 and older pay half the regular one-way fare with a Medicare card or other ID showing their birth date. Seniors with ID who buy on the train skip the $5 surcharge. Call Metro-North at 212-532-4900 to confirm the rule for weekday morning trains.

Sources: 

## Senior transportation in Rockland County: every ride, town by town

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/senior-transportation-rockland-county-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Rockland has a county senior bus, free TOR buses right now, a Clarkstown town bus and trains into New Jersey. Here is what each one costs, who can ride, and which towns it reaches.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How can my dad in Pearl River get to his doctor if he stops driving?
A: He can apply for Regular TRIPS, the county's curb-to-curb bus for Rockland residents 60 and older who find the regular bus hard to use. Once approved, call 845-364-8747 on a weekday between 7:30 am and 5 pm, ideally two business days ahead. If he can still walk to a stop, TOR buses are free for now. If he has Medicaid, Medical Answering Services (866-932-7740) arranges free rides to medical visits with 72 hours notice.

Q: Is there a senior bus for my mom in New City or Nanuet?
A: Yes. Clarkstown Mini Trans runs five routes that meet at the Nanuet Mall, Monday to Friday 6:55 am to 8:05 pm and Saturday 9 am to 7:10 pm, for a $0.40 senior fare. The town also gives weekday door-to-door rides to Clarkstown senior clubs and from senior complexes to supermarkets. Call 845-623-0667. TRIPS covers New City and Nanuet as well.

Q: Are TOR buses really free?
A: For now, yes. Rockland County's fares page says fare collection continues to be waived and rides on TOR and TRIPS remain free, with no end date. When fares return, the senior fare for riders 60 and older is $1.00, and Medicare card holders get the same discount.

Q: How far ahead do I book TRIPS?
A: You can request a ride up to 14 days ahead, and the county recommends at least 48 hours (two business days). Requests are taken by phone only, Monday to Friday, 7:30 am to 5 pm, at 845-364-8747. Voicemail requests are not honored.

Q: What does a senior pay on the train from Suffern or Spring Valley into New Jersey?
A: Riders 65 and older pay half the regular one-way fare on NJ TRANSIT trains to and from Metro-North stations such as Suffern, Sloatsburg, Spring Valley, Nanuet and Pearl River. Show a Medicare card or another ID with a birth date. Seniors who buy on board with ID skip the $5 surcharge. Call Metro-North at 212-532-4900 to confirm the rule for weekday morning trains.

Q: Does Medicaid pay for my parent's rides in Rockland?
A: Yes, for medical appointments. Call Medical Answering Services at 866-932-7740, or book at medanswering.com, at least 72 hours ahead. Medicaid does not cover trips to pharmacies or grocery stores. Fidelis members in Rockland have booked through the same number since April 1, 2026.

Sources: 

## Senior transportation in Westchester: every ride option, town by town

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/senior-transportation-westchester-county-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

Westchester has a half-price Bee-Line fare, a $5 ParaTransit van, and more than 20 town and village senior ride programs that many families never hear about. Here is who runs what, what it costs and how to book.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How can my mom in Yonkers get to her doctor if she stops driving?
A: If she can walk to a stop, the Bee-Line costs $1.50 with a Medicare card or Half-Fare ID. If she cannot use the bus, apply for Bee-Line ParaTransit at 914-995-7272 (press 3); rides cost $5 within three quarters of a mile of a Bee-Line route. TRA gives free medical rides to adults 60 and older at 914-764-3533. You can also ask the Yonkers Office for Aging (914-963-4411) about local rides.

Q: Is there a senior bus for my dad in Ossining or Briarcliff Manor?
A: Yes. The Ossining Senior Center runs a Wednesday 12:30 pm bus to the Croton ShopRite for seniors who eat lunch at the center first, for $2. It also sells discount taxi coupons to Ossining and Briarcliff residents 60 and older at $3 each, up to 15 a month, for use around Ossining, Briarcliff, the Croton ShopRite and Phelps Hospital. Call 914-762-1350.

Q: Does being over 65 qualify someone for Bee-Line ParaTransit?
A: No. ParaTransit is only for people who are functionally unable to use the regular Bee-Line bus. Age alone does not qualify, and neither does a disability by itself. Riders 65 and older who can use the bus get the $1.50 reduced fare instead.

Q: How far ahead do I book Bee-Line ParaTransit?
A: Up to 7 days ahead, by phone at 914-995-7272 (press 1), Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm. Next-day trips must be booked by 5 pm. You can also book online or in the ParaTransit app. Cancel at least 2 hours before the trip.

Q: Can seniors use the reduced fare on Metro-North at rush hour?
A: Mostly yes. The reduced fare, half the one-way peak fare for riders 65 and older, works at all times except on weekday morning trains arriving at Grand Central between 6 and 10 am. It is valid in the evening rush.

Q: Does Medicaid pay for rides in Westchester?
A: Yes, for medical appointments. Call Medical Answering Services at 844-666-6270, or book at medanswering.com, at least 72 hours ahead. Medicaid does not pay for trips to pharmacies or grocery stores.

## When a parent dies in New York: the first days and weeks

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/when-a-parent-dies-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

The first week is mostly phone calls and paperwork, and most of it can wait a day or two. Here is what has to happen first, who to tell, and when the Surrogate's Court comes in.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How do I get my dad's death certificate in Brooklyn?
A: Ask the funeral director to order certified copies when you make arrangements. You can also order from the NYC Health Department through VitalChek online, by mail or in person at 45 Lafayette Street by appointment. Each copy costs $15 plus a processing fee: $9.30 online, $7.50 by mail or $2.75 in person.

Q: My mom died in Albany. Who do I tell first?
A: Choose a funeral home and give the director her Social Security number so it can report the death to Social Security, which also tells Medicare. Then call her pension, banks and insurers, and mail a copy of the death certificate to the DMV. If she had Medicaid, tell the Albany County Department of Social Services.

Q: Can I report a death to Social Security online?
A: No. Social Security accepts death reports by phone or in person only. Usually the funeral home reports it. If not, call 1-800-772-1213 (TTY 1-800-325-0778), Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.

Q: Do we have to return my father's last Social Security payment?
A: Yes, if it was for the month he died. Social Security says benefits received for the month of death and any later months must be returned. If you aren't sure which payment that covers, ask Social Security.

Q: What is the small estate limit in New York?
A: Personal property with a gross value of $50,000 or less, not counting property set aside by law for a surviving spouse or children under 21. Real estate in the parent's name alone means you need probate or administration instead.

Q: How much do death certificates cost outside New York City?
A: From the NYS Department of Health, $30 a copy by mail or $45 a copy online or by phone, plus a vendor fee per order. You can also order from the local registrar where the death happened.

Sources: 

## Volunteering for older New Yorkers: programs and stipends

URL: https://seniorsofny.com/article/volunteering-older-adults-ny/
Updated: 2026-11-26

From tutoring kids for a small stipend to counseling neighbors on Medicare, New York has volunteer roles for every schedule. Here is where to sign up in the city, the state and the counties near New Jersey.

### Key facts



### Questions

Q: How can my mom find volunteer work in Rockland County?
A: If she is 55 or older, call the Rockland Senior Volunteer Program (RSVP) at the county Office for the Aging, 845-364-2112. It matches volunteers with local agencies for roles like meal delivery, food pantries, library help and museum guiding, with insurance and optional mileage reimbursement for drivers.

Q: Where can my dad volunteer with older adults in Manhattan?
A: Call NYC Aging's Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 or sign up on the NYC Aging volunteer portal. Roles include Friendly Visiting, Medicare counseling through HIICAP, blood pressure checks and fitness classes at older adult centers, and one-day shifts at food pantries and resource fairs.

Q: Do Foster Grandparent volunteers get paid?
A: They get a small stipend. In New York City, NYC Aging pays Foster Grandparents $4 an hour, tax-free, for service and training time. Volunteers must be 55 or older, meet income rules and give at least 15 hours a week.

Q: Can I volunteer to help people with Medicare questions?
A: Yes. The Health Insurance Information, Counseling and Assistance Program (HIICAP) trains volunteers across New York. Use the interest form at aging.ny.gov/volunteer, or call your county office. In Orange County, call 845-615-3715. Insurance marketers can't serve as HIICAP counselors in New York City.

Q: How old do you have to be for AmeriCorps Seniors?
A: You must be 55 or older for RSVP, the Foster Grandparent Program and the Senior Companion Program. Use the AmeriCorps Seniors Pathfinder tool on americorps.gov to find openings near you.

Q: Can I volunteer in a New York state park?
A: Yes. More than seventy state parks and historic sites have Friends Groups that run volunteer projects. You can also join I Love My Park Day each spring (it was May 2 in 2026), or call your local park and ask how to help.
